stories.headline: Cabinet clears bill raising Lok Sabha and Assembly seats 50% in every state
stories.dek: The Constitution amendment bill lifts the Lok Sabha ceiling to 850 and keeps each state's share of seats unchanged until 2051, as the government makes a second attempt after April's defeat.
stories.summary: The Union Cabinet on Friday approved a Constitution amendment bill raising seats in the Lok Sabha and state Assemblies by 50% to implement women's reservation. The House ceiling would rise from 550 to 850, with state shares frozen until 2051.
body: The Union Cabinet, chaired by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, on Friday approved the Constitution (132nd Amendment) Bill, which raises Lok Sabha and state Assembly seats by 50% in every state and Union territory.
The bill is meant to put into effect 33% reservation for women in the Lok Sabha and state Assemblies. It will be taken up at a special sitting of Parliament that begins on Monday, November 30.

The bill raises the Lok Sabha's maximum strength from 550 to 850. Up to 815 members would come from states, up from 530, and 35 from Union territories, up from 20. The cap on a state Assembly would rise from 500 to 650 members. The House now has 543 members.

Because every state's seats go up by the same proportion, each state keeps its present share of the House. The bill keeps the resulting allocation and boundaries in place until 2051. Deccan Herald gave Karnataka as an example: its seats would rise from 28 to 42, of which 14 would be reserved for women.

A separate Delimitation (Second) Bill sets out how boundaries would be redrawn. The Centre would appoint a commission headed by a current or former Supreme Court judge, with the Chief Election Commissioner or a nominated Election Commissioner and the relevant State Election Commissioner as members. Its final orders would have the force of law and could not be challenged in court. The bill uses the latest published Census, which is the 2011 Census.

Women's reservation would take effect after the first delimitation held once the amendment comes into force, which points to the 2029 Lok Sabha elections. Seats reserved for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes would be included within the women's quota. The bill does not change the Rajya Sabha or state legislative councils.

The government's earlier attempt failed on April 17, when the Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill received 298 votes for and 230 against. It needed two-thirds of members present and voting, which was 352. The opposition said the promise of a uniform increase had been made in speeches but was not written into the bills. The ruling side said the opposition's stand harmed women's empowerment.

The ruling National Democratic Alliance still lacks a two-thirds majority on its own. The DMK and the Sharad Pawar-led Nationalist Congress Party have said their support will depend on safeguards for states' proportional representation. A 50% rise and a 25-year freeze were among the DMK's demands.
The Lok Sabha meets on November 30 and December 1, and the Rajya Sabha on December 2 and 3.
keyFacts: The Lok Sabha ceiling would rise from 550 to 850: 815 for states and 35 for Union territories.
State Assemblies could have up to 650 members, up from 500.
Women's reservation would run for 15 years from the commencement of the 106th Amendment Act, 2023, unless Parliament extends it.
The April bill got 298 votes for and 230 against; 352 were needed.
The Rajya Sabha sits on December 2 and 3 under the special sitting plan.
stories.background: The story so far: Parliament passed the women's reservation law in 2023, linking it to a Census and delimitation. In April 2026 the government brought the 131st Amendment Bill to raise the Lok Sabha ceiling to 850. Southern states feared losing share to the more populous north. On April 17 the bill fell short of a two-thirds majority, and two linked bills were withdrawn. The new bill writes the 50% rise and the freeze till 2051 into the text.
stories.whatNext: The Constitution amendment bill is to be tabled in the Lok Sabha on Monday, November 30, with the sitting expected to end on December 3.

stories.headline: Election Commission fixes website flaw that exposed voters' personal details and ID paths
stories.dek: The fault was in a feature that lets logged-in voters request a call from their local electoral officer. Researchers said it could have been used to collect data in bulk.
stories.summary: The Election Commission of India fixed a website flaw that could have exposed voters' personal details and the file paths of uploaded identity documents. Reuters found the fault and told the commission on October 26; it is not known whether anyone exploited it.
body: The Election Commission of India has closed a gap on its website that could have revealed voters' private information and the locations of identity documents they uploaded, after Reuters raised it with the commission.

The flaw mattered to voters because any of India's roughly 1 billion voters can log in to the site with a voter ID or mobile number. It was found in the call-booking feature, which lets a logged-in voter ask for a call from the local electoral officer. The feature was introduced in June 2025.

Reuters said that when a voter requested a call, the network tab in the browser's developer tools showed the reference number of the form the voter had submitted to enrol or update details. Using that number to book a call then displayed the user's name, contact numbers and email, birth date and home address. It also showed file paths to documents such as passports. None of this appeared on the main screen.

A Reuters reporter was able to download a copy of his own national identity card by following the steps. Security researchers Karan Saini and Ehraz Ahmed retraced the steps on the site and said the form reference numbers followed a predictable sequence. They said this could let someone guess the numbers and automate requests to collect data in bulk.

The researchers said an ordinary user was unlikely to stumble on the information, but a person with basic coding knowledge could use it. "The server only appeared to check whether a user is logged in, not whether they're authorised to see a particular document," Saini said.

Reuters said it sent its findings to the commission and its three commissioners on October 26 and received no response. On Thursday, a commission spokesperson said its information technology division had been asked to look into the findings. Hours later, Reuters and the two researchers found that personal details and file paths were redacted, and the researchers said the change effectively blocked the method.
Reuters said it could not determine whether the flaw had been exploited, how long it had existed or how many voters might have been affected. The BJP did not respond to its request for comment.

Pawan Khera, a spokesperson for the Congress, called the findings "deeply alarming". He said exposure of voters' personal information could enable "targeted intimidation, profiling, voter suppression and the manipulation of vulnerable communities".
Ashok Lavasa, a former election commissioner, said the flaw appeared to be inadvertent. "You don't collect all this information so that you can put it in the public domain," he said.
The commission's privacy policy says it makes "reasonable efforts" to protect data but that "no system can be guaranteed to be completely secure".
keyFacts: Reuters reported the flaw to the Election Commission and its three commissioners on October 26.
The call-booking feature in which the flaw was found was introduced in June 2025.
Researchers Karan Saini and Ehraz Ahmed confirmed the flaw and the later fix.
Reuters could not say whether the flaw was exploited or how many voters were affected.
stories.background: In 2019, researcher Karan Saini found that the commission's online voter search portal exposed some voters' personal details through the browser's network tab. That flaw was fixed after media reports. The Hindu reported in October that a civic-tech group's audit found access to certain voter details could be switched on or off centrally for state election officials.

stories.headline: Supreme Court orders Thiruparankundram lamp lit on November 28, suspends temple trustees
stories.dek: The bench said Tamil Nadu's failure to follow its November 20 order was wilful disobedience and issued contempt notices to the Chief Secretary, the police chief and other officials.
stories.summary: The Supreme Court on Friday ordered the Karthigai Deepam lit at the disputed stone pillar on Thiruparankundram hill on November 28 and suspended the temple's trustees. It issued contempt notices to top Tamil Nadu officials, and the next hearing is on December 15.
body: The Supreme Court on Friday ordered the Karthigai Deepam lit on the disputed stone pillar on Thiruparankundram hill in Madurai on November 28, and suspended the Subramaniya Swami Temple's board of trustees.
The order affects devotees, the temple and the state administration. It also puts senior Tamil Nadu officials under contempt proceedings, which are action for disobeying a court order.

A bench of Justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul M Pancholi appointed two retired judges, S Vaidyanathan and V Parthiban, as receivers to run the temple trust. They must ensure the lamp is lit, in consultation with the temple's hereditary priests. The Central Reserve Police Force will take charge of security on the hill.

The bench changed its November 20 order, which had allowed only a small team to light the lamp. Members of the public may now light lamps, at least 50 metres from the Sikandar Badusha Dargah on all sides. The CRPF must also ensure that Muslim worshippers can reach the dargah and pray without obstruction.

The court said the trustees' resolution that they would not follow its order showed "wilful and flagrant disobedience". It said the officials "seem to have acted at the dictates of their political bosses". Justice Kumar said no person, however high, could defy a Supreme Court order.

Notices went to the Chief Secretary, the Director General of Police, the Endowments Secretary and Commissioner, the Madurai Collector, the Police Commissioner, the Superintendent of Police and temple authorities. They must appear in person on December 15 and say why contempt action should not follow.
The Chief Secretary must file a personal affidavit within 10 days. It must set out emails, calls and messages exchanged between officials about the lamp and the November 20 order.

The petitioners argued that the trustees, named on November 13, were political appointees used as cover for the state. The Collector's counsel said he had done what he could. Solicitor General Tushar Mehta, appearing for the Archaeological Survey of India, called the conduct "administrative arrogance".

Prime Minister Narendra Modi welcomed the order, and the BJP said the state government had acted against Hindus. Former Chief Minister M K Stalin blamed Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay for the escalation, calling it a threat to communal harmony.
The court said its order did not create rights for any party and was limited to the contempt petitions. The main case on religious rights will be heard in the second week of January 2027.
keyFacts: Receivers S Vaidyanathan and V Parthiban will run the temple trust after the board's suspension.
Public may light lamps at least 50 metres from the Sikandar Badusha Dargah.
The Chief Secretary has 10 days to file an affidavit on official communications.
Petitioners' counsel said the trustees were appointed on November 13.
The main case will be heard in the second week of January 2027.
stories.background: The story so far: A devotee, Rama Ravikumar, went to the Madras High Court after the temple refused to light the Karthigai Deepam at the pillar near the dargah. A single judge ordered it on December 1, 2025, and a Division Bench upheld that on January 6, 2026. The state appealed. On November 20 the Supreme Court allowed a one-time lighting on November 24. The lamp was instead lit at the customary Deepa Mandapam. The state says the pillar is a British survey stone.
stories.whatNext: The Chief Secretary and other officials must appear before the Supreme Court on December 15, the next hearing date.

stories.headline: NCP(SP) says it will back delimitation bill; DMK sets conditions as Kharge calls Opposition meeting
stories.dek: The Congress called the NCP(SP) decision unfortunate, while the DMK said it stands by two demands on Tamil Nadu's share of seats before it decides.
stories.summary: The NCP(SP) said on Friday it will vote for the delimitation bill, and the DMK indicated it could do so if Tamil Nadu's share of seats is kept. Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge has called Opposition floor leaders to a meeting on Saturday.
body: The Nationalist Congress Party (Sharadchandra Pawar) said on Friday that it will support the delimitation bill in Parliament, though it is part of the Opposition INDIA bloc, which mostly opposes the plan.

The votes matter because a constitutional amendment needs a two-thirds majority, and the ruling National Democratic Alliance does not have that in either House. A similar bill failed in the Lok Sabha in April. Delimitation is the redrawing of constituency boundaries and the fixing of seat numbers.

Party leader Jitendra Awhad spoke in Mumbai after meeting Sharad Pawar, who is in hospital. "We will support the delimitation Bill. We will attend the INDIA Bloc meeting," he said. He said Supriya Sule and the party's eight MPs had decided to back the bill and that this was final.

Awhad said he and Pawar had not discussed the party's official stand as such. "The general point being discussed was that delimitation is a constitutional process. It will have to be done at some point," he said. The party has issued a whip, a written order to attend and vote, asking its MPs to be in Delhi. Sule will reach Delhi on Monday.

Congress leader Sachin Sawant called the decision "deeply unfortunate" in a post on X. He said it helps the Modi government's "authoritarian mindset". Shiv Sena (UBT) MP Sanjay Raut said earlier that those who vote for the bill would be "traitors to the nation".

In Chennai, DMK chief M K Stalin said the party stands firm on two demands. They are keeping Tamil Nadu's 7.18 per cent share of Lok Sabha seats in an expanded House, and extending for another 25 years the freeze on each state's share of seats, set on the 1971 Census. "There is no change in our position, and there is no question of any compromise," he wrote on X.

DMK, which has 22 Lok Sabha MPs, has convened a meeting of its MPs at 10 am on Saturday. Congress leader Karti Chidambaram said the DMK would have to explain a "complete U-turn" if it backed the bill. Stalin attacked the Congress in his statement, calling those who abandoned principles for power "shameless and ungrateful".

Kharge, Leader of Opposition in the Rajya Sabha, has invited Opposition floor leaders to his residence at 11:30 am on Saturday. The DMK, AAP and BJD, which are outside the INDIA bloc, have also been invited. Congress general secretary K C Venugopal said the party is approaching all Opposition parties.
The Union Cabinet on Friday approved the Constitution Amendment Bill. Congress's Jairam Ramesh said the bills had not been shared with MPs by 6 pm on Friday.
keyFacts: The NCP(SP) has eight Lok Sabha MPs and one Rajya Sabha member.
The DMK has 22 Lok Sabha MPs and eight in the Rajya Sabha.
Lok Sabha meets on November 30 and Rajya Sabha on December 2; sittings end on December 3.
Kharge's meeting is at 11:30 am on Saturday at 10 Rajaji Marg.
Sanjay Raut said parties voting for the bill would be recorded as traitors.
stories.background: A constitutional amendment bill on delimitation and women's reservation was defeated in the Lok Sabha in April 2026 after the Opposition voted against it. The government withdrew two linked bills. The DMK left the INDIA bloc in May after the Congress allied with the TVK in Tamil Nadu. The Cabinet cleared a fresh bill on Friday, with a special sitting from November 30. The NCP(SP), which voted against in April, now says it will support it.

stories.headline: Bengal police collect papers from voters deleted in SIR; Supreme Court tells petitioners to go to High Court
stories.dek: The state's poll office says it knows nothing of the exercise, while opposition parties call it illegal and a police officer describes it as routine.
stories.summary: West Bengal police have been visiting homes and holding camps to check documents of voters deleted in the SIR. On Friday the Supreme Court told petitioners to raise the matter in the Calcutta High Court, where a forum says it will file next week.
body: West Bengal police are collecting documents from voters removed from the electoral rolls in the special intensive revision (SIR), and the Supreme Court on Friday told petitioners to take the issue to the Calcutta High Court.

The deleted voters include many of the 22 lakh people who have appealed to SIR tribunals to get their names back. Nearly 91 lakh electors, about 12% of the state's voters before the revision, were removed from the rolls.

The Hindu reported that a copy of an order shows the Director-General and Inspector-General of the police's Law and Order unit held a video conference on Monday, November 23, with district police chiefs. They were asked to examine data on deleted voters across all 294 Assembly constituencies and to send a report by November 30.

Police teams have since visited homes, the paper reported, and held camps at government schools in Howrah. A senior police officer said it is a routine exercise. A police superintendent told Scroll the district intelligence branch was collecting information such as birth certificates and voter rolls. He declined to say whether there was a government order, and said nothing would be done on the basis of the information.

Additional Chief Electoral Officer Arindam Niyogi said the Election Commission did not "have any knowledge about any such drive". Director General of Police Siddhinath Gupta said: "I don't know about any forms being filled up." An unnamed state government official said police may verify whether a person is an Indian citizen.

Opposition leaders say police carry forms asking for names, addresses, voter ID numbers, birth or school certificates, land papers and whether parents appear on the 2002 rolls. Congress leader Prasenjit Bose said the form has no government letterhead or Election Commission stamp. He has written to Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari, calling the deployment "unwarranted and arbitrary" and a contempt of the Supreme Court's order.

Counsel Gopal Sankaranarayanan and Prashant Bhushan told the bench led by the Chief Justice of India that the police acted without the Election Commission's involvement. The court asked them to approach the High Court.

The All Bengal Joint Forum to Safeguard the Right to Vote, which includes the CPI(M), Trinamool Congress, Congress and CPI(ML) Liberation, will file a petition next week. Advocate Jhuma Sen called the police action "absolutely illegal". Trinamool called it intimidation.
Garga Chatterjee of Bangla Pokkho said a police reporting format had separate columns for Hindu and Muslim applicants. The sources do not carry a police response to that claim.
keyFacts: Police order asked district officers to submit reports by November 30.
The Supreme Court said on Monday that appeals from 22 lakh of 38 lakh appellants be prioritised.
Camps were held at government schools in Howrah, The Hindu reported.
Trinamool MP Samirul Islam wrote to the Chief Election Commissioner seeking intervention.
Opposition leaders say the exercise began on Tuesday in several districts.
stories.background: The SIR in Bengal ran from October 2025 to February 2026, before the April Assembly election. Nearly 91 lakh electors were deleted. Tribunals set up after a Supreme Court order on March 10 hear appeals. In May the court upheld the SIR but said the Election Commission cannot decide citizenship. On Monday it ordered faster hearings and more tribunals. New this week: police checks on deleted voters.
stories.whatNext: The joint forum says it will file a petition in the Calcutta High Court next week, and police district reports are due by November 30.

stories.headline: Ex-CJI Gavai writes to President, alleges collegium favours one community in judicial appointments
stories.dek: In a three-page letter dated November 27, the former Chief Justice cited government data on low numbers of SC, ST, OBC and minority judges in the high courts.
stories.summary: Former Chief Justice of India B.R. Gavai has written to President Droupadi Murmu alleging that the Supreme Court collegium is favouring one community in appointments and transfers. He cited data showing few SC, ST, OBC and minority judges in the high courts.
body: Former Chief Justice of India Bhushan R Gavai has written to President Droupadi Murmu urging her to intervene over what he called the favouring of one community in recommendations for higher judiciary posts.

The letter bears on who sits on India's constitutional courts. Gavai said Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, Other Backward Classes, minorities and women remain thinly represented among judges. The collegium is the group of senior Supreme Court judges that recommends judges for the Supreme Court and the high courts.

The three-page letter is dated November 27. Copies went to Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Law Minister Arjun Ram Meghwal. Gavai said he wrote as a concerned citizen who had been both a member and the head of the collegium.

He wrote that candidates from "one particular section of the society" were being favoured, to the exclusion of others, including marginalised groups and forward-caste candidates outside that section. He did not name the community. He wrote that a community under 5 per cent of the population has had over 40 per cent representation in the Supreme Court, a share that has risen "manifold in the recent past". People aware of the matter told Hindustan Times and Outlook the reference was to Brahmins.

Gavai cited the law minister's March 2025 reply in the Rajya Sabha. It showed that 715 high court judges had been appointed since 2018. Of these, 22 were from Scheduled Castes and 16 from Scheduled Tribes.
The same reply showed 89 judges from OBCs and 37 from minorities. Roughly three in four came from the general category.

For appointments between January 2021 and January 2026, he said, forward communities held close to 80 per cent, while OBCs got under 14 per cent. He said caste is not recorded for Supreme Court appointments and called that silence part of the problem.

He also questioned transfers of high court chief justices, without naming anyone. He said one chief justice was moved between smaller high courts and then recommended for a prominent one. He said a "meritorious and hard-working" chief justice was moved to a smaller court to make way.
Gavai said he was part of the collegium for some of those decisions. "Each of us bears some share of the failure," he wrote. He withheld the reasons, citing propriety.
He headed the collegium from May 14 to November 23, 2025. Under it, 129 names were recommended for high court posts, and the government cleared 93, according to Supreme Court data.
The 129 included 10 Scheduled Caste candidates and 11 from OBC and backward classes. They also included 13 from minorities and 15 women.

The present collegium has CJI Surya Kant and Justices Vikram Nath, BV Nagarathna, MM Sundresh and PS Narasimha. Gavai did not name Kant. Neither the Supreme Court nor the government had responded publicly to the letter.
keyFacts: Gavai's letter is three pages long and dated November 27, 2026.
He cited a Rajya Sabha reply of March 2025 on 715 high court appointments since 2018.
He said OBCs received under 14 per cent of appointments between January 2021 and January 2026.
Gavai's collegium recommended five Supreme Court judges, including Justices NV Anjaria and Vijay Bishnoi.
stories.background: Gavai was the 52nd Chief Justice of India, from May 14 to November 23, 2025, and the second from the Scheduled Castes. He was succeeded by Surya Kant. The collegium system, under which senior judges recommend judges, grew out of three Supreme Court rulings between 1981 and 1998 and has been criticised as lacking transparency.

stories.headline: Millions of wives in South Asia lack legal protection from marital rape, study finds
stories.dek: The study by Samaj, a coalition of women's rights groups, says India, Sri Lanka and Bangladesh still exempt husbands from rape laws; Supreme Court hearings in India begin on December 9.
stories.summary: A study by the South Asian coalition Samaj says millions of married women in the region lack full legal protection against marital rape. India, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka and Afghanistan have not criminalised it, and India's Supreme Court begins final hearings on December 9.
body: A study by Samaj, a coalition of women's rights groups in South Asia, has found that millions of married women in the region are not fully protected by law from rape by their husbands.
The finding matters in India, where 10 petitions challenging the marital rape exception are pending before the Supreme Court. The court is due to begin final hearings on December 9.

The study says India, Afghanistan, Sri Lanka and Bangladesh have not criminalised marital rape. Only the Maldives punishes it on par with other forms of rape, it says. More than 100 countries worldwide have made it a crime. The UK changed its law in 1991.

Ranjeeta Silwal of Equality Now, a global women's rights group that is part of Samaj, said the laws largely come from British colonial rule. The exception dates to 1860 in India and Bangladesh and 1885 in Sri Lanka. It lists sex by a man with his adult wife as an exception to rape.

"The idea comes from the belief that consent for sex is implied in marriage, that marriage is a threshold where consent ends," Silwal told the BBC. Campaigners say forced sex is rape whoever commits it.

Pakistan removed the exception in 2006, but no higher court has confirmed that rape laws apply within marriage, the study says. A recent high court ruling gave husbands broad protection against prosecution for non-consensual sex.

In Afghanistan, the Taliban have rolled back women's protections since returning to power in 2021. Under a penal code introduced in January, Silwal said, a husband can be prosecuted for violence against his wife only if he causes a broken bone, an open wound or severe bruising. The punishment on conviction is 15 days in prison. The code does not mention marital rape.

Nepal and Bhutan have criminalised marital rape but set lighter penalties. In Bhutan, the offence carries one month to one year. In Nepal, rape carries six to 20 years, but a husband faces up to five years.

In India, courts have given differing rulings. Some judges have called the law outdated and urged Parliament to change it. The Indian government, religious groups and men's rights organisations oppose the petitions, saying criminalisation would be "excessively harsh".

Silwal said opponents argue that criminalising marital rape would undermine the family and affect religious and cultural values. They also fear false accusations against men. She added that a change in law may not by itself bring justice to survivors.
keyFacts: Samaj is a coalition of women's rights groups in South Asia.
The Maldives is the only South Asian country that punishes marital rape on par with other rape.
Pakistan removed its marital rape exception in 2006.
Bhutan's penalty for marital rape is one month to one year.
Ten petitions are pending in India's Supreme Court.
stories.background: India's exception to rape for sex between a man and his adult wife dates to 1860. Courts have given conflicting rulings on it over the years, and the government has opposed petitions to remove it. Last year a court's decision to free a man whose wife died after he raped her drew public anger.
stories.whatNext: The Supreme Court is due to begin final hearings on the 10 petitions on December 9.

stories.headline: India's reservoir storage 32% below last year; southern states worst hit
stories.dek: Southern reservoirs hold 37.52% of capacity, the lowest of five regions, while western India recorded the largest weekly fall in volume, Central Water Commission data show.
stories.summary: Water in India's 178 major reservoirs stood at 60.19% of live capacity in the Central Water Commission's bulletin of 26 November, nearly 32% below last year. Southern India is worst affected, and only the east gained over the week.
body: India's 178 major reservoirs held 111.209 billion cubic metres (BCM) of water on 26 November, 31.64 per cent less than a year earlier, the Central Water Commission (CWC) said in its weekly bulletin.

The figure matters for farms, towns and power plants that depend on stored water through the dry months. Storage is also 21 per cent below the normal level for this time of year, which the commission puts at 140.770 BCM.

The reservoirs were at 60.19 per cent of live storage capacity, down from 61.56 per cent a week earlier, when they held 113.748 BCM. Last year's level was 162.688 BCM. Live storage is the water that can actually be drawn out of a reservoir. The 178 reservoirs have a combined live capacity of 184.762 BCM.

Southern India is worst off. Its 50 reservoirs, across Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Kerala, Tamil Nadu and Telangana, held 20.964 BCM, or 37.52 per cent of capacity. That compares with 85.69 per cent a year ago and a normal level of 71.94 per cent. The region lost 0.630 BCM over the week.

Western India recorded the largest weekly fall in volume. Its 58 reservoirs in Goa, Gujarat and Maharashtra dropped from 27.188 BCM to 26.367 BCM, a loss of 0.821 BCM. They stand at 68.30 per cent of capacity, against 95.29 per cent last year and a normal 82.01 per cent.

Central India lost 0.801 BCM. Its 28 reservoirs in Chhattisgarh, Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh and Uttarakhand held 37.521 BCM, or 77.22 per cent of capacity. Last year the figure was 90.32 per cent, and the normal level is 79.32 per cent.

In the north, 11 reservoirs across Himachal Pradesh, Punjab and Rajasthan held 10.165 BCM, or 51.25 per cent of capacity. They lost 0.401 BCM in a week. A year ago they were at 83.91 per cent, and the normal level is 70 per cent.

Eastern India was the only region to gain. Its 31 reservoirs rose by 0.114 BCM to 16.192 BCM, or 74.10 per cent of capacity. That is still below last year's 80.04 per cent and the normal 75.42 per cent.
keyFacts: The 178 reservoirs monitored have a combined live capacity of 184.762 BCM.
They account for 71.67 per cent of India's total known live reservoir capacity.
Storage fell by about 2.54 BCM in one week.
Central India lost 0.801 BCM, the second-largest weekly decline.
All five regions are below both last year's and normal levels.
stories.background: The Central Water Commission is a technical body under the Ministry of Jal Shakti. It advises on and coordinates the control, conservation and use of water resources, and publishes a weekly bulletin on storage in major reservoirs.

stories.headline: Canada's Supreme Court largely upholds Quebec ban on religious symbols for public workers
stories.dek: The court ruled 6-1 that Quebec may shield Bill 21 from most rights challenges, but said courts can still declare such laws incompatible with the Charter.
stories.summary: Canada's Supreme Court on Friday largely upheld Quebec's Bill 21, which bars many public-sector workers from wearing religious symbols. Muslim groups criticised the ruling, while Quebec's premier called it a victory for secularism.
body: Canada's Supreme Court on Friday largely upheld Quebec's Bill 21, a 2019 law that bars many public-sector workers from wearing religious symbols on the job.

The law covers teachers, police officers, lawyers and judges. It affects Muslim, Sikh, Jewish and Christian Canadians who wear items such as a hijab, turban, kippah or cross. The ruling also matters to other provinces, which were watching how far governments may go in using the "notwithstanding clause", a part of the constitution that lets them override certain rights.

The court ruled 6-1 that Quebec could protect the law from most challenges based on the Charter of Rights and Freedoms. Chief Justice Richard Wagner wrote that Bill 21 "is rooted in Quebec's legitimate and historical commitment to ensuring the laicity of the state in a free and democratic society".

The court did find that one part of the law infringes democratic rights. That part stops elected members of Quebec's National Assembly from taking part in its work if they wear a face covering for religious reasons.

In a 4-3 decision, the court also said lower courts may declare that a law breaches the Charter even when the notwithstanding clause lets it stand. It did not make such a declaration in this case. It rejected most arguments that the law broke parts of the Charter that the clause cannot override.

Justices Andromache Karakatsanis, Michelle O'Bonsawin and Nicholas Kasirer dissented on parts of the decision. They wrote that the clause "cannot be used to authorize laws that are incompatible with the fundamental character of Canada as a free and democratic country". They said the law infringes freedom of religion, freedom of expression and equality rights.

Quebec Premier Paul St-Pierre Plamondon, whose Parti Québécois leads the government, called the ruling "a victory for Quebec's secularism, which is a distinct and unique model compared to the rest of Canada".

Stephen Brown, chief executive of the National Council of Canadian Muslims, said: "Entire categories of people are now barred from entire sectors of employment, not because of what they have done, but because of who they are." He said the law had pushed many Muslim women out of teaching.

The chair of the English Montreal School Board, one of the main challengers, said the board was "obviously very disappointed". Prime Minister Mark Carney said his government would study the ruling and that legislatures should respect the rights of all Canadians, including minorities.
The hearings ran four days and drew 51 interveners, including six attorneys general. The court's 520-page judgment was released on Friday morning.
keyFacts: The ruling was 6-1 on the main question of shielding Bill 21 from most Charter challenges.
Quebec passed Bill 21 in 2019 and invoked the notwithstanding clause in advance.
Fifty-one interveners took part, including six attorneys general.
The court split 4-3 on lower courts' power to issue declarations on shielded laws.
Quebec's Court of Appeal upheld the law in February 2024.
stories.background: Quebec passed Bill 21 in 2019, invoking the notwithstanding clause before any court challenge. A Quebec Superior Court judge upheld most of it in April 2021 while describing its effects as "cruel". The Court of Appeal upheld it in February 2024. Muslim, Sikh and Catholic teachers and school boards were among those who challenged it. Earlier this year Quebec also passed a law extending secularism rules to subsidised daycares and post-secondary institutions.
stories.whatNext: Carney said his government would study the ruling's implications; no date for any further step was given.

stories.headline: Tamil Nadu police arrest TVK MLA Arul Vignesh over woman collector's harassment complaint
stories.dek: The arrest of the Kallakurichi legislator came four days after a case was registered, following Madras High Court directions; a separate case has been filed against a DMK MLA.
stories.summary: Tamil Nadu police arrested Kallakurichi MLA C Arul Vignesh of the ruling TVK on Friday over a woman district collector's complaint of sexual harassment. He has denied the allegations, calling them false and politically motivated.
body: Tamil Nadu police on Friday arrested C Arul Vignesh, the 36-year-old Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) MLA from Kallakurichi, over a sexual harassment complaint by a woman district collector.

The case involves an IAS officer who heads a district and a legislator from the party that governs the state. The Madras High Court has been monitoring the police investigation and has ordered a final report by December 22.

Police said a team led by Shristi Singh, Superintendent of Police, Tiruppur, took him into custody from his residence. N Kamini, Inspector General of Police (Administration), is supervising the probe. In a statement, police said the complainant and other witnesses were questioned before the arrest and the investigation is continuing.

The officer's complaint was received on November 23, and a case was registered at the Kallakurichi All Women Police Station that day. She alleged that Vignesh sent obscene WhatsApp messages, made unwanted advances and tried to visit her official residence at night.

He is booked under the Tamil Nadu Prohibition of Harassment of Women Act and sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita covering sexual harassment, stalking and use of force against a public servant. Vignesh has denied the allegations.

DMK MP Kanimozhi Karunanidhi raised the matter publicly on November 9. The government had maintained that no complaint had been received. On November 23, State Public Prosecutor R John Sathyan told the High Court that neither the Chief Secretary nor the police had received one. The complaint was filed after the court asked about it, and the state changed its position at the hearing on November 24.

Kanimozhi wrote on X after the arrest: "At last, it happened." AIADMK general secretary Edappadi K Palaniswami called the arrest delayed action. DMK president MK Stalin alleged that ministers and allied leaders tried to shield the MLA, and demanded action against them.
Police said 201 social media posts about the incident had been removed. They asked the public not to share material that goes against the High Court's directions on publishing details of the case.

Separately, police registered a case against DMK MLA Vasantham Karthikeyan, who represents Rishivandiyam, on a complaint by a senior woman officer of the Tamil Nadu State Rural Livelihoods Mission. The alleged incident took place on October 18, and police received the complaint on November 26.
keyFacts: Police said the complaint was received on November 23 and registered as Cr No. 91/2026.
The Tamil Nadu government has set up a four-member Internal Complaints Committee headed by Additional Chief Secretary Kakarla Usha, with 60 days to inquire.
The National Commission for Women took suo motu cognisance and sought an impartial inquiry.
Opposition Leader Udhayanidhi Stalin met Governor Rajendra Arlekar on Thursday and demanded a CBI probe.
Vasantham Karthikeyan, 47, is booked under BNS sections 79, 132 and 351(2).
stories.background: DMK MP Kanimozhi Karunanidhi raised the allegations on November 9, about three months after the reported incidents. The government initially said no complaint had been made. After the Madras High Court questioned the state on November 23, the officer lodged a complaint and the court ordered a probe led by a senior IPS officer.

stories.headline: Madras High Court rejects Vijay's plea to dismiss Perambur election petition
stories.dek: A separate bench barred bypolls to Tiruchi East, the seat Vijay vacated, and two others until election petitions are decided, but allowed two bypolls.
stories.summary: The Madras High Court on Friday refused to throw out a voter's election petition against Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay's Perambur win. A division bench also barred bypolls in three seats, including Tiruchi East, while clearing two others.
body: The Madras High Court on Friday dismissed Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay's application to reject an election petition challenging his victory in the Perambur Assembly seat.

The ruling means the case goes to trial, and Vijay's election from Perambur stays under challenge. A separate order the same day affects voters in five constituencies where bypolls had been stayed since July 10.

Justice V Lakshminarayanan held that the petition by S Dinesh, a Perambur voter, discloses a cause of action and can be maintained. The judge said the alleged omissions and discrepancies in Vijay's nomination affidavit were specifically pleaded. Their significance, he said, could be judged only after evidence is examined.

Dinesh alleged that Vijay's affidavit left out two property deals made in early 2026: a ₹30 crore land purchase at Panruti in January, and a ₹35 crore sale of a commercial property at Padi a month later. He also said a 50-cent plot in Kodaikanal, declared as agricultural land, is classed as government land in revenue records.
Dinesh argued that this deprived voters of information and amounted to undue influence, a corrupt practice under Section 123(2) of the Representation of the People Act, 1951.

Vijay denied the allegations. His lawyers said the petition lacked the material facts needed to sustain a challenge. They said he had declared assets of more than ₹600 crore and that the alleged discrepancies did not show how voters' choices were influenced.

Vijay, who leads the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK), won Perambur with 1,20,365 votes, beating the DMK's RD Shekar by 53,715 votes. He also won Tiruchi East and gave it up to keep Perambur. Shekar and another voter, TN Lakshmi Narasimhan, have filed separate petitions against the Perambur result.

In the second case, a bench of Chief Justice Sushrut Arvind Dharmadhikari and Justice G Arul Murugan barred the Election Commission of India from holding bypolls to Tiruchi East, Viralimalai and Karur until pending petitions are decided. It allowed bypolls to Ambasamudram and Perundurai.

The court held that a seat cannot be filled by bypoll while an election petition still asks for a declaration that the petitioner or another candidate won it. Such a bypoll could leave two people claiming the same seat, it said. The restriction applies only where a petition actually makes such a claim.

The court also accepted the Commission's position that deferring the bypolls does not breach the time limit under Section 151-A of the Act. It rejected a request to direct the Commission to notify the three bypolls at once.

The petitioner in that case, K Venkatachalapathy of Tirunelveli, had argued that bypolls could produce two claimants to one seat. Vijay told the court that an indefinite delay would leave lakhs of voters without elected representatives. He called the petition a proxy fight for defeated candidates.

The Tamil Nadu government argued that a vacancy arises once the Speaker accepts a resignation, and that a later petition cannot undo it. The Commission told the court it did not plan bypolls in the five seats until the petitions were decided.
keyFacts: Justice V Lakshminarayanan decided the Perambur plea; the bypoll case was heard by a bench led by Chief Justice Dharmadhikari.
Vijay resigned Tiruchi East on May 10; the Speaker accepted it that day.
DMK's S Inigo Irudayaraj filed his Tiruchi East petition on June 17, 2026.
The interim stay on bypolls to five seats was issued on July 10.
Bypolls to Ambasamudram and Perundurai are cleared.

stories.headline: US disables ship leaving Iran as Tehran vows to break naval blockade
stories.dek: An adviser to Iran's Supreme Leader said the Strait of Hormuz will stay shut, while President Trump named the Pickaxe Mountain nuclear site as a target if strikes resume.
stories.summary: The US military said it disabled a Palau-flagged commercial ship that left Bandar Abbas despite its blockade of Iranian ports. Iran said it would not reopen the Strait of Hormuz or accept the blockade.
body: The US military said on Friday that aircraft disabled a commercial ship on Thursday in the Gulf of Oman after it tried to run Washington's blockade of Iranian ports.
The blockade and Iran's closure of the Strait of Hormuz affect shipping through one of the main sea routes out of the Gulf. Neither side has signalled that it will back down.

The US Central Command said the Palau-flagged M/V Pacific Archer left the Iranian port city of Bandar Abbas despite multiple warnings. Military aircraft fired precision munitions that struck the ship's stern, it said. The vessel's propulsion was disabled. The command said the civilian crew was unharmed.

Mohammad Mokhber, an adviser to Iran's Supreme Leader Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei, responded in remarks carried by Iranian state media. "Neither will the Strait of Hormuz be reopened, nor will we allow the blockade to remain in place," he said. He did not say how Iran planned to break the blockade.

Separately, US President Donald Trump told reporters at his Mar-a-Lago residence in Florida on Thursday that the US would hit Iran's Pickaxe Mountain nuclear facility if it took any new military action. "If we did anything, we would absolutely hit Pickaxe Mountain, but we haven't seen any real activity there," he said.

Pickaxe Mountain is a fortified underground site near Iran's Natanz uranium enrichment complex. Trump said Iran's air force and navy had been wiped out and that Tehran had not been able to restart work at nuclear sites the US had earlier struck. He said Iran was being given every chance to make a deal.

Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi told the state news agency IRNA that Tehran remained open to talks but was focused on resilience against pressure and on keeping trade routes running. He said Qatar and Pakistan were still mediating and passing proposals to Tehran.
In a separate interview, Araghchi accused Israel of making claims about Iran to create the conditions for another war and to draw the US into it. He said Iran was ready to defend itself.
keyFacts: The ship was struck on Thursday, November 26, in the Gulf of Oman.
The US reimposed its naval blockade on Iranian ports in July.
Earlier this month the US announced Task Force Iron Gate to restrict weapons and sanctioned materials moving across Iran's land borders and the Caspian Sea.
Qatar and Pakistan are carrying proposals between the sides, Araghchi said.
stories.background: The story so far: The US reimposed a naval blockade on Iranian ports in July, during a conflict in which it has struck Iranian nuclear sites. Iran has kept the Strait of Hormuz closed. Earlier this month Washington announced Task Force Iron Gate to curb arms and sanctioned goods crossing Iran's land borders and the Caspian Sea. Qatar and Pakistan are mediating. The latest events are the disabling of the Pacific Archer and Trump's remarks on Pickaxe Mountain.

perspectives.summary: The US military says it enforces the blockade and warned the ship repeatedly before striking it. Trump says victory is within reach, that Iran is being given a chance to deal, and that Pickaxe Mountain would be hit if strikes resume.

stories.headline: Goyal says India-US trade deal is close to culmination
stories.dek: The commerce minister spoke days after the US proposed 25% tariffs on Indian goods, to be capped at 17% if the two countries sign a deal.
stories.summary: Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal said on Friday that the India-US trade deal is close to culmination. The US has proposed 25% tariffs on Indian goods, falling to 17% if a deal is agreed.
body: Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal said on Friday that the proposed India-US trade agreement is close to culmination, days after Washington proposed higher tariffs on Indian goods.

The deal matters to Indian exporters because the US buys more from India than any other trading partner. Under the US proposal, tariffs on Indian goods would be 25%, but capped at 17% if a deal is reached.

Goyal spoke virtually at a debt capital market summit. "The US trade deal is close to culmination," he said. "The process and pathway, which was always something which held back finalising the deal, is now taking some shape."

US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer announced the proposal on Wednesday. It follows a Section 301 investigation, a US probe into trade practices. The probe alleges that India and other countries run surplus factory capacity in a way that harms American industry. The 25% rate is the second-highest among 14 countries covered. Vietnam faces the highest proposed levy, at 35%.

The proposals are not in force. The new tariffs face public consultation before taking effect next year. Public hearings are scheduled to begin on January 25, 2027, and a final decision is likely only after that.

The two countries have been negotiating since reaching an interim accord in February. India has sought US market access for textiles, pharmaceuticals and engineering goods. Washington has pushed for greater access for American products and closer alignment on trade rules.

Brokerage Jefferies said in an equity strategy report that the tariff threats are likely to push India to speed up a deal. A 17% tariff would give India an edge of 1 to 3 percentage points over countries such as Bangladesh, Indonesia, Malaysia, Thailand and Vietnam.

Haresh Calcuttawala, co-founder and chief executive of the trade platform Trezix, said the announcements add to uncertainty for exporters. "The proposals are not in force yet. Comments are due in January, and hearings follow, so the real operational challenge for the next few months is uncertainty," he said. He said small exporters would be hit harder.
Trade expert Abhijit Das has argued that India should not sign an asymmetric deal and should tell the US it can live with higher tariffs, as it has for the past year and a half.

Goyal also said nine free trade agreements covering 38 developed countries had been concluded in the past four-and-a-half to five years. On the India-EU agreement, he said it was expected to be signed later this year, with implementation likely by March or April 2027.

stories.headline: IBM ends US visa and green card sponsorship for most consulting roles
stories.dek: Staff in the company's largest division can take a post outside the US or leave by December 31, with three months' severance.
stories.summary: IBM has stopped sponsoring US work visas and green cards for most roles in IBM Consulting, its largest division. Employees on Blind say affected staff must move abroad or leave by the end of the year.
body: IBM will no longer sponsor US work visas or green cards for most roles in IBM Consulting, its largest division, which has more than 150,000 employees, the company said in a statement.

The change matters to Indian workers, who are the largest group of H-1B visa holders. The H-1B lets US companies hire foreign workers for specialised jobs for a limited time. A green card lets a foreign citizen live and work in the US permanently.

IBM said its use of such programmes has been falling for several years. "As skill availability and client needs have evolved, we have opted to discontinue visa and green card sponsorship for the majority of such roles in IBM Consulting," the company said. It gave no further details and did not link the decision to US government action.

Employees say those affected were told to choose between an IBM job outside the US and leaving by the end of the year. Posts on Blind, an anonymous workplace forum, say some were given about three weeks to decide. Those who decline an overseas role would get three months' severance, with December 31 as their last day.

One employee wrote on Blind that they were told they had three weeks to choose between "an 80 per cent pay cut to relocate to India or losing my job by December 31". Several employees said they heard of the change in one-on-one meetings with managers. These accounts have not been independently verified.
IBM's careers portal on November 19 listed 1,278 consulting vacancies outside the US. Of these, 1,125 were in India. The portal showed 89 consulting openings in the US.

Federal filings show IBM won a little over 1,600 H-1B approvals in fiscal 2026. That was down from more than 2,000 in FY2025. In FY2024 it was almost 3,000. The counts cover the whole company and include extensions for current staff.
US President Donald Trump extended the $100,000 fee on employers for H-1B workers in September 2026. He said the 2025 fee had cut H-1B registrations by large IT outsourcing firms by 92%.

In October, the US suspended several firms, including Cognizant, Infosys, Tata Consultancy Services, Microsoft and Adobe, from the permanent labour certification process used for green card sponsorship.
The National Foundation for American Policy says Indians receive about three-quarters of H-1B visas.

stories.headline: Delhi Police rescue 164 Indonesians and Malaysians held in cyber fraud racket
stories.dek: Police said the foreign nationals had their passports taken on arrival and were made to cheat people in their home countries; one Malaysian man has been arrested.
stories.summary: Delhi Police Crime Branch said it rescued 92 Indonesians and 72 Malaysians who were allegedly trafficked to India on false job offers and forced into online investment fraud. A Malaysian man has been arrested, and two Indian men are being sought.
body: Delhi Police said on Thursday that they rescued 164 foreign nationals, 92 Indonesians and 72 Malaysians, who were allegedly held against their will and forced to run an online investment fraud from the Delhi area.
The case shows how people from abroad can be lured to India with job offers and then made to defraud others. Police said the targets were mainly people in Malaysia and Indonesia.

Police said the group was promised well-paid jobs and had their passports taken when they arrived. They were then moved into paying guest accommodation. A senior officer said those who refused to work were beaten, and that police knew of about two such cases so far.

The officer said about 40 cabs carried the group between their lodgings and the call centre, and they were not free to move on their own. Police said the group were given written scripts and told to create fake female profiles on social media. They would build online relationships and then persuade targets to put money into fake trading platforms and apps.

The Crime Branch acted on an email alert received about a week earlier. Special Commissioner of Police (Crime Branch) HGS Dhaliwal said he set up a specialised team. Police first believed 60 to 70 people were held, but the number found at the premises in Dwarka was far higher.

Police arrested Tan Guan Wei, a 25-year-old Malaysian from Negeri Sembilan, who is being questioned about his role. Two men, Sunil Kumar and Sushil Bhati, are absconding, the officer said. Police said Bhati arranged the lodgings and transport, and that bank accounts linked to both men paid rent and other costs.
Police seized 355 mobile phones, 168 desktop computers, 26 laptops, 53 SIM cards and 174 passports, along with servers. Of the passports, 95 were Indonesian and 79 Malaysian.

Dhaliwal said the conditions in which the people were held were deplorable. He said police would help the rescued foreigners return home safely. A case has been registered at the Crime Branch police station under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, and police are looking into how the group was recruited and brought to India.
keyFacts: Police found 164 people, though first information pointed to 60 to 70.

Of the 53 SIM cards, 31 were international and 22 Indian.
About 40 cabs were allegedly used to move the group between lodgings and the call centre.
Police are examining bank accounts linked to Sunil Kumar and Sushil Bhati.
stories.background: Cyber fraud complaints have risen sharply in India. Figures from the National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal show 2.8 million complaints in 2025, with losses of about 22,495 crore rupees. The federal government has said most cases involved fake investment and trading scams. In July, Lucknow Police arrested 119 people after raiding a fake international call centre.

stories.headline: Allahabad High Court quashes UP PCS-2025 prelims results, orders fresh merit list and mains
stories.dek: Justice Manish Kumar Nigam held that the commission did not follow reservation norms when it drew up category-wise results, affecting 4,533 reserved-category candidates named in the petition.
stories.summary: The Allahabad High Court on Friday quashed the UP PCS-2025 preliminary results and told the Uttar Pradesh Public Service Commission to prepare a revised merit list and hold the mains again. The petitioners said high-scoring reserved-category candidates were wrongly kept out of the open list.
body: The Allahabad High Court on Friday quashed the preliminary examination results of the Uttar Pradesh Public Service Commission's PCS-2025 recruitment and ordered a revised merit list and a fresh mains examination.

The ruling affects every candidate in the recruitment cycle. The mains examination and interviews already held will not count towards final selection, the petitioners' counsel said. Candidates who qualify in the revised prelims results must sit the mains again.

Justice Manish Kumar Nigam disposed of a writ petition filed by Sanjay Kumar and three other OBC and EWS candidates from Prayagraj. OBC stands for Other Backward Classes and EWS for Economically Weaker Sections. The court held that the commission had not followed established reservation norms when preparing the category-wise results. The prelims results were declared on December 1, 2025.

The petitioners' counsel argued that the commission kept 4,533 meritorious reserved-category candidates within their own categories, although they scored above the general cut-off. The group comprised 2,993 OBC, 464 Scheduled Caste, 155 Scheduled Tribe and 921 EWS candidates.

The petitioners said this breached Articles 14 and 16 of the Constitution and section 3(6) of the Uttar Pradesh Public Services (Reservation for Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes and Other Backward Classes) Act, 1994. They said it kept deserving candidates from qualifying for the mains.

Abhishek Shukla, counsel for the petitioners, said the commission had limited the open category to candidates who had not sought reservation. He said the court rejected that reading. "Open category signifies 'open to all'. It is not a quota or a fixed slot; it cannot be subjected to rigid compartmentalisation," Shukla said.
Under the migration principle, reserved-category candidates who meet the open-category merit standard can be considered for open seats. Shukla said the court upheld it.
The petition also challenged the commission's office memorandum of January 9, 2020. The court noted that the memorandum had already been quashed in a separate matter concerning the APO examination.
The commission has not been quoted on the ruling.
keyFacts: The prelims results were declared on December 1, 2025.
The petitioners named 4,533 reserved-category candidates they said were kept out of the open list.
The petition was filed by Sanjay Kumar and three other OBC and EWS candidates from Prayagraj.
The commission's office memorandum of January 9, 2020 had already been quashed in the APO examination case.
stories.background: The Uttar Pradesh Public Service Commission is the state body that recruits candidates for the Provincial Civil Service and other government posts through competitive examinations. The dispute concerns how it applied the migration principle when drawing up the open-category list from the preliminary examination.
stories.whatNext: The commission must now publish revised prelims results and a fresh merit list, then hold the mains afresh; the sources give no dates.

stories.headline: Supreme Court warns Rajasthan of contempt action over river pollution
stories.dek: A two-judge bench called the state's response "absolutely lethargic" and said officers and the government would face consequences if no concrete action plan is produced.
stories.summary: The Supreme Court on Friday criticised Rajasthan for its slow response to pollution in the Jojari, Bandi and Luni rivers and warned of suo motu contempt proceedings against officials. The case is listed for orders on December 10.
body: The Supreme Court on Friday warned Rajasthan that it could start contempt proceedings on its own against state officials over delays in tackling pollution in the Jojari-Bandi-Luni river system.

The rivers flow through Jodhpur, Pali and Balotra before they meet near Balotra. The court also raised the acute drinking water shortage in Balotra, which affects people living along the polluted rivers.
A bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta was hearing a case it had taken up on its own. It described the state's response as "absolutely lethargic".

The bench told Additional Solicitor General S V Raju, who appeared for Rajasthan: "You better advise the government and let them come out at the ground level and work rather than facing the wrath of this court."

The court said it would not let the matter slide because of red tape or bureaucratic hurdles. "If positive action and positive blueprint will not come, your officers will suffer. Not only officers, it will reflect upon the government as a whole," it said.

Senior advocate Balbir Singh, who is assisting the court as amicus curiae (a friend of the court), referred to its October 26 order. That order stopped Rajasthan from granting fresh permissions for industrial units along or near the rivers until the high flood line and buffer zones are scientifically fixed.

The amicus also told the court that a special investigation team has been formed to look into organised illegal bajri (sand and gravel) mining affecting the three rivers and their tributaries. The state's status report said some FIRs had been registered.

On the water shortage in Balotra, the bench suggested a pipeline of about 100 km from the Narmada canal. "If the central and the state government will be able to do this, it will be a wonderful thing for the people of that area," it said.

The court had earlier set up two bodies. In November last year it created a high-level ecosystem oversight committee to find the causes of pollution, supervise remedial work and suggest long-term fixes. In August it told Rajasthan to form an Integrated Coordination Group headed by the chief secretary for time-bound action.
The matter will be heard again on December 10 for orders.
keyFacts: The Jojari, Bandi and Luni rivers flow through Jodhpur, Pali and Balotra and meet near Balotra.
An October 26 order bars fresh industrial permissions near the rivers until flood lines and buffer zones are fixed.
A special investigation team is probing organised illegal bajri mining on the rivers and their tributaries.
The court suggested a pipeline of about 100 km from the Narmada canal for Balotra.
stories.background: The Supreme Court is hearing the river pollution case on its own motion. In November last year it set up a high-level oversight committee on the river ecosystem. In August this year it ordered Rajasthan to form an Integrated Coordination Group under the chief secretary. On October 26 it barred fresh industrial permissions near the rivers.
stories.whatNext: The court has listed the case for orders on December 10.

stories.headline: RBI issues final rules for banks to hold suspected money-mule accounts
stories.dek: The directions set a uniform, time-bound procedure for temporary debit holds and take effect on July 1, 2027, or earlier if a bank chooses.
stories.summary: The Reserve Bank of India has issued final amendment directions on suspected money-mule accounts used in cyber-enabled frauds. Banks must follow a standard procedure for temporary debit holds, effective July 1, 2027, or earlier at a bank's option.
body: The Reserve Bank of India has issued final amendment directions that set a standard procedure for banks to place temporary debit holds on accounts suspected of money-mule activity linked to cyber-enabled fraud.

A money mule is a person whose account is used to move money obtained through fraud. The rules affect bank customers across the country, and the RBI said the procedure is meant to protect genuine customers from inconvenience.

The procedure is described as uniform and time-bound. Under it, banks can place a hold on an amount or an account on their own initiative, known as suo moto action, when they suspect a link to money-mule activity or cyber fraud. The holds are to be removed in coordination with law enforcement agencies.

The central bank issued a draft of the directions on September 11, 2026, to seek feedback from stakeholders. It said it examined the feedback and incorporated modifications in the final text. A statement on the feedback received is given in an annex to the release.
The directions come into force on July 1, 2027. A bank may apply the procedure from an earlier date if it chooses.

The RBI issued separate amendment directions, under its Know Your Customer rules, for each category of bank. These cover commercial banks, small finance banks, payments banks, local area banks, regional rural banks and urban co-operative banks.

Directions take effect on July 1, 2027, or earlier at a bank's option.
Six categories of banks are covered, from commercial banks to urban co-operative banks.
The RBI release number is 2026-2027/1584.
stories.background: The RBI's Know Your Customer directions set the checks banks must carry out on their customers. The new amendments add a procedure for acting on accounts suspected of being used to route money from cyber-enabled frauds.

stories.headline: Rupee falls 60 paise to 92.98 against dollar as Sensex drops 989 points
stories.dek: Higher crude oil prices after attacks on Saudi oil facilities and profit-taking in IT stocks and HDFC Bank ended a two-day rise in Indian markets on Friday.
stories.summary: The rupee settled 60 paise lower at 92.98 against the dollar on Friday, and the Sensex fell 989.33 points to 83,339.26. Profit-taking and rising crude oil prices ended a two-day rally.
body: The rupee lost 60 paise to settle at 92.98 against the US dollar on Friday, while the Sensex fell 989.33 points, or 1.17 per cent, to close at 83,339.26.

The falls hit both currency and share markets on the same day. A weaker rupee makes imports, including oil, costlier, and a fall in the Sensex cuts the value of equity holdings. Brent crude, the global oil benchmark, rose to about $97 a barrel.

In the interbank foreign exchange market, the rupee opened at 92.44 and touched a low of 93.01 before settling at 92.98 (provisional). On Thursday it had closed at 92.38, according to The Hindu's figures. Another outlet put the previous close at 92.4450.

Anuj Choudhary, research analyst at Mirae Asset Sharekhan, said crude rose after Houthi forces attacked an Aramco facility in Saudi Arabia. He said month-end dollar demand might also press the rupee, and expected the pair to trade between ₹92.65 and ₹93.20.

The Nifty fell 277.30 points, or 1.07 per cent, to 25,607.20. The Sensex lost as much as 1,120.26 points during the day. HCL Tech, Infosys, Tata Consultancy Services, Bajaj Finserv, Tech Mahindra and Axis Bank were among the biggest losers on the Sensex. Bharat Electronics, Titan, InterGlobe Aviation, Tata Steel, Power Grid and Trent gained.

Vinod Nair, head of research at Geojit Investments, said higher crude, a weaker rupee and rising domestic bond yields prompted profit booking in heavyweight stocks after a strong four-week rally. He said a revival in Asian AI stocks could also divert some money away from India.

Foreign institutional investors bought equities worth ₹5,843.33 crore on Thursday, according to exchange data. Kaveri More of Choice Broking said record foreign equity inflows of $15.16 billion in November had supported the rupee and let the RBI rebuild its foreign exchange reserves.

Asian markets rose on Friday. South Korea's Kospi gained 4.34 per cent and Japan's Nikkei 225 gained 2.11 per cent. Broader Indian markets did better than the benchmarks: the Midcap 150 and Smallcap 250 indices rose by up to 0.52 per cent each, The Economic Times reported.
On Thursday the Sensex had closed at 84,328.59 after a gain of 390.31 points. Analysts quoted by The Hindu put the dollar index at 103.77 on Friday, up 0.16 per cent.
keyFacts: The rupee touched a day's low of 93.01 against the dollar on Friday.
Brent crude traded at about $97.2 a barrel, up roughly 0.6 to 0.8 per cent.
The rupee's lowest-ever close is 96.88, recorded on October 8.
Foreign equity inflows reached a record $15.16 billion in November, according to Choice Broking.
Choudhary expects the rupee to trade between ₹92.65 and ₹93.20.
stories.background: The rupee hit a record closing low of 96.88 against the dollar on October 8 and has since recovered nearly 5 per cent. Indian shares rallied for much of November on strong foreign buying, before Friday's fall.

stories.headline: Supreme Court declines urgent hearing on plea against Ranbir Kapoor's Ramayana
stories.dek: Justice Joymalya Bagchi told the petitioner's lawyer to make a film of his own if he has a different view of the epic.
stories.summary: The Supreme Court on Friday refused to list urgently a petition challenging Ramayana: Rise of a Legend, which has been in theatres since November 5. The bench said the film was already released and the matter would be heard in due course.
body: The Supreme Court on Friday declined to list for urgent hearing a petition against the Ranbir Kapoor-starrer Ramayana: Rise of a Legend, saying those with a different view of the epic can make their own film.

The film has been running in theatres since November 5. The petition alleges that its makers distorted mythological facts, and it challenges the certification the Central Board of Film Certification gave the film.

A bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana heard the matter when the petitioner's counsel mentioned it. The lawyer said the plea was registered on November 23 and had not yet been listed.
"The movie has already been released. Those who wanted to watch it have already seen it," the Chief Justice said.
The counsel argued that "many facts are distorted" and said, "It is a new generation which is coming."

Justice Bagchi questioned the need to come to court over how a film reads the epic. "They made a movie as they understand, you make a movie as you understand. Don't waste the time of the court. If you have a counter view about the epic, make a movie based on that," he said.
The lawyer kept pressing for an early date. The Chief Justice said the court was concerned only with urgency, which he said was absent because the film was in theatres and people were watching it.

"People can have their own view. There's no doubt about it. There may be somebody who will praise, somebody will say something critical. This is perfectly respectable," he said. The bench said the matter would be listed in due course.

The petition, filed by Manoj Singh Thakur, is titled Manoj Singh Thakur v. Union of India. It names as respondents the producers Prime Focus Studios and Monster Mind Creations, producer Namit Malhotra, actor Yash, director Nitesh Tiwari, screenplay writer Sridhar Raghavan and dialogue writer Shreyas Jain.

The film, also called Ramayana: Part 1, stars Ranbir Kapoor as Rama, Sai Pallavi as Sita and Yash as Ravana. Its cast also includes Sunny Deol, Lara Dutta, Arun Govil, Kajal Aggarwal, Rakul Preet Singh and Vivek Oberoi.
keyFacts: The plea was registered on November 23 under Diary No. 72618/2026.

The film is directed by Nitesh Tiwari and produced by Namit Malhotra.
The bench comprised CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana.

stories.headline: Calcutta HC sets aside Ritabrata Banerjee's appointment as Leader of Opposition
stories.dek: Justice Krishna Rao told Speaker Rathindra Bose to decide afresh within 10 days, a deadline that falls around December 7, after the winter session opens on December 4.
stories.summary: The Calcutta High Court set aside the Speaker's June 3 decision naming Ritabrata Banerjee Leader of the Opposition and Akhruzzaman chief whip. The Speaker must decide afresh within 10 days, and the winter session may open without a recognised opposition leader.
body: The Calcutta High Court on Friday set aside the West Bengal Speaker's June 3 decision to appoint rebel Trinamool Congress MLA Ritabrata Banerjee as Leader of the Opposition and Akhruzzaman as chief whip.

Justice Krishna Rao directed Speaker Rathindra Bose to reconsider both posts in accordance with law within 10 days. The winter session of the Assembly begins on December 4 and runs until December 14, and the deadline falls around December 7. The House could therefore open without a recognised Leader of the Opposition.

The court was hearing a petition by Sobhandeb Chattopadhyay, a Trinamool MLA. The party's general secretary, Abhishek Banerjee, had written to the Speaker on May 9 naming him for the post. The party said 70 MLAs backed him.

Ritabrata Banerjee and MLA Sandipan Saha questioned that resolution. They said they had not agreed to Chattopadhyay's appointment and alleged that some signatures were not genuine. The party expelled both on June 1. The Speaker recognised Ritabrata Banerjee on June 3 after a rival group of 58 MLAs backed him.

The court held that the Speaker had not checked the disputed signatures with all 70 members. It said Chattopadhyay and the party were not given a chance to respond, while the rival group was heard. It also noted that the Speaker knew of the expulsion when he made the appointment. The court said the Speaker should have examined the party constitution and made an independent enquiry instead of treating a faction's numbers as decisive.

The court said the pending dispute at the Election Commission over the party's name and symbol did not bar judicial scrutiny. It did not appoint Chattopadhyay and did not say how the Speaker should settle the rival claims.
Chattopadhyay said he could not recall any earlier case of the Assembly having no Leader of the Opposition. He also criticised remarks by state Health Minister Sharadwat Mukhopadhyay.

Trinamool MP Kalyan Banerjee said the ruling was a matter of serious constitutional concern, not of celebration. He said the Speaker had failed to act above political affiliations. He also alleged that Ritabrata Banerjee kept the post and its benefits after an earlier Division Bench order allowing him to continue provisionally lapsed on October 18.
A former MLA who has been elected to the Assembly eight times said the Speaker is supreme in the House. He said there is no provision for a floor test to pick a Leader of the Opposition.
keyFacts: Trinamool won 80 of the 294 seats in the May Assembly election.
The winter session runs from December 4 to December 14.
An earlier Division Bench order let Ritabrata Banerjee continue provisionally until October 18.
The Election Commission has recognised his group as the Democratic Trinamool Congress, with the Envelope symbol.
stories.background: The Trinamool lost power to the BJP in the May 2026 election and then split. A group led by Ritabrata Banerjee claims to be the real party. The Election Commission has allotted separate names and symbols to the two sides, Mamata All India Trinamool Congress and Democratic Trinamool Congress. The rebels say they are the real Trinamool and have sought its name and symbol, which the Mamata Banerjee camp challenges.
stories.whatNext: The Speaker must decide on both posts within 10 days of receiving the order, a deadline falling around December 7, while the winter session begins on December 4.

stories.headline: Fashion brands move most of $254 million in orders from Bangladesh to India
stories.dek: Three factory owners said Zara, H&M and other buyers diverted the orders between November 1 and 18 as strikes disrupted garment production in Bangladesh.
stories.summary: Global fashion brands shifted about $254 million worth of orders out of Bangladesh in the first 18 days of November, with most going to India, three factory owners said. Indian textile shares rose on the news.
body: Global fashion brands diverted about $254 million worth of orders from Bangladesh between November 1 and 18, with most going to India, three factory owners said.

The shift matters in India because Indian textile makers are the main gainers. Shares of Gokaldas Exports rose as much as 11% and Trident gained about 5%. Welspun Living, KPR Mill and Vardhman Textiles rose around 2% each.

The owners said Zara, H&M, Marks & Spencer, Celio and other brands moved orders. The sum is nearly a tenth of Bangladesh's monthly orders, they said. They spoke on condition of anonymity, citing their ties with international buyers. Zara's owner Inditex declined to comment. M&S, H&M and Celio did not respond to requests for comment.

Garment workers have been protesting over pay. The Bangladesh Garment Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BGMEA) said the protests have caused more than $400 million in production losses. Garments account for more than 80% of Bangladesh's export earnings and nearly 40% of its manufacturing jobs.

On Wednesday, Bangladesh approved a 36% rise in the minimum wage for garment workers, the smallest in four decades. Workers had demanded more than double. Fresh clashes with police followed. Abdur Rahman Tarafder, secretary of the Ministry of Labour and Employment, called the rise "satisfactory" and said he hoped all garment workers would return to work from Saturday.
Industry leaders said the rise would narrow Bangladesh's labour-cost advantage over India. Union groups argue the wages remain low by global industry standards.

BGMEA director M. Mohiuddin Chowdhury said buyers now put delivery times ahead of price. He said India can offer a delivery advantage of about a week, and Vietnam and Cambodia up to 15 days. Rival hubs typically deliver in 60 to 90 days, against about 120 days in Bangladesh, he said.

Energy shortages have also hit output, and factories around Dhaka have lost an estimated 20 to 25 production days. BGMEA president Mahmud Hasan Khan declined to name brands. He said moving some orders elsewhere for a time helps the industry keep global clients while limiting losses.

Khan Monirul Alam, managing director of Alps Apparels Group, said most of his buyers had stopped placing orders since November 1. Chowdhury warned that shifted orders might not return. "Brands have options. They will not wait for us if instability persists," he said.
keyFacts: Brands also looked to Vietnam, Cambodia and Indonesia to cut supply-chain risks, industry leaders said.
Bangladesh is the world's second-largest apparel exporter after China.
Factories around Dhaka have lost an estimated 20 to 25 production days.
Some Bangladeshi factories are considering overtime and costly air freight to meet delivery dates.
stories.background: Bangladesh's garment industry has faced pay protests, energy shortages and political uncertainty. Tension over former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina's possible return to Dhaka from India has added to worries about more disruption.
stories.whatNext: The labour ministry's Tarafder said he hoped all garment workers would resume work on Saturday.
