stories.headline: Bombay High Court lets Tata Sons board meet on November 30, refuses Trusts' plea
stories.dek: Justice Abhay Ahuja said any outcome of the meeting would be subject to the court's final orders; the next hearing is on January 18, 2027.
stories.summary: The Bombay High Court refused urgent relief to two Tata Trusts that wanted the November 30 Tata Sons board meeting deferred or Chairman N Chandrasekaran barred from voting. The court said the meeting can go ahead, with its outcome subject to final orders.
body: The Bombay High Court on Friday refused urgent relief to two Tata Trusts that sought to defer the November 30 Tata Sons board meeting or stop N Chandrasekaran from casting a vote there.

The ruling matters to the group's owners and its investors. The meeting is expected to take up stock exchange listing of Tata Sons, a possible restructuring to keep it private, and an extraordinary general meeting (EGM), a special meeting of shareholders.
A bench of Justice Abhay Ahuja said: "We are not granting any relief today. Let the meeting (on November 30) go on as per schedule. Any outcome of the meeting would be subject to our final orders."

The Sir Dorabji Tata Trust (SDTT) and the RD Tata Trust (RDTT) filed two suits on Thursday against Tata Sons and six of its directors. They challenge the September 17 board resolution reappointing Chandrasekaran as executive chairman for a third five-year term.

The suits say the resolution was invalid because it lacked the affirmative vote Article 121 of the Articles of Association requires. SDTT seeks ₹50 crore and RDTT ₹15 crore in damages, with 18% annual interest.

Justice Ahuja asked why the meeting should be deferred or Chandrasekaran barred from voting, since he already holds the post in his second term. He said other agenda items could be heard and decided separately.

Senior counsel Abhishek Manu Singhvi, for SDTT, said the Reserve Bank of India deadline cited by Tata Sons was a ploy to show fake urgency. He argued that Noel Tata, who chairs Tata Trusts, did not vote in favour on September 17, so there was no majority. He said the third term takes effect on February 27, 2027.
Senior counsel Aspi Chinoy, for RDTT, called the reappointment decision "perverse".

Senior counsel Harish Salve, for Tata Sons, said the board must meet because the RBI has set a December 12 deadline for Tata Sons to inform it of its decision on mandated listing. He said any resolution would be subject to the court's orders.

Salve also argued that with only two trust nominees there could never be a majority, so the matter had to go to a casting vote. He said the trusts had not asked for deferment in their interim application, and that "the two trustees cannot paralyse the company".
The court ordered Tata Sons and the other respondents to file reply affidavits. Tata Trusts holds about 66% of Tata Sons.
keyFacts: Justice Abhay Ahuja heard the plea on Friday, a day after the suits were filed.
Tata Sons told the court the RBI has set a December 12 deadline on listing.
Chandrasekaran's third term is due to take effect on February 27, 2027, Singhvi told the court.
The Trusts' suits name Tata Sons and six of its directors as defendants.
stories.background: The story so far: N Chandrasekaran told the Tata Sons board on August 12 that he would not seek another term. On September 17 he said he had reconsidered, and the board reappointed him 4:1, over Noel Tata's objection. The Trusts said on September 20 that the vote was not valid. SDTT and RDTT sued on November 26, and the court declined urgent relief on November 27.

stories.headline: Bangladesh Speaker says Dhaka may take Hasina's extradition from India to the ICJ
stories.dek: Hafiz Uddin Ahmed, visiting Pakistan, also said Sheikh Hasina would go straight to jail if she returned, and that he did not expect her to come back for 10 years.
stories.summary: Bangladesh's Parliament Speaker Hafiz Uddin Ahmed said Dhaka may approach the International Court of Justice if India does not extradite Sheikh Hasina. Hasina has said she will return on December 16; Dhaka says she would be arrested.
body: Bangladesh may approach the International Court of Justice (ICJ) if India does not extradite former prime minister Sheikh Hasina, Parliament Speaker Hafiz Uddin Ahmed has said.

The remark bears on relations between two neighbours that share a 4,096km border. Hasina, 79, has lived in India since fleeing Dhaka in August 2024 after a student-led uprising ended her 15-year rule. Her spokesperson, Syed Mozammel Ali, has said she plans to return on December 16, Bangladesh's Victory Day.

Ahmed made the remarks during a six-day visit to Pakistan, in comments reported by BBC Urdu on Thursday. He said Hasina would have to go straight to jail if she returned. He also said her announcement was meant to keep her supporters motivated and that she would not return for the next 10 years.

Ahmed also alleged that Bangladesh had effectively become a "colony" of a neighbouring country over the past 15 years, without naming one. He said India "did not help the Bengalis but played a role in weakening Pakistan" in 1971, and that Kashmir should be resolved in line with UN resolutions.

A special tribunal in Dhaka sentenced Hasina to death in her absence over the crackdown on protesters during the 2024 uprising. The UN says as many as 1,400 people were killed by security forces. Hasina has denied wrongdoing and questioned the legitimacy of the trial. Her Awami League party is banned in Bangladesh.

On Thursday, Humaiun Kobir, Bangladesh's state minister for foreign affairs, told reporters that Hasina had become a "thorn" in ties with India. "She will come only through the extradition treaty. It is not a matter of her returning; she will be handed over," he said.

India's foreign ministry said on Wednesday that Dhaka's extradition request was being examined through established legal processes. Its spokesperson, Randhir Jaiswal, said a voluntary return by Hasina would be a separate matter.

Hasina's aide Abu Obaidha Arin told the BBC she could travel on a commercial flight or cross the land border if Dhaka did not arrange a flight. He said supporters had identified nine possible crossing points and could mobilise five million people to welcome her.
keyFacts: Hasina's spokesperson says she plans to return to Bangladesh on December 16, Victory Day.
Hasina was sentenced to death in absentia by a special tribunal over the 2024 crackdown.
Tarique Rahman, Bangladesh's prime minister since February, has not visited India despite an invitation.

The BNP won the February 2026 election, from which the Awami League was barred. India has acknowledged Dhaka's requests but announced no decision.

stories.headline: RBI cuts daily CRR maintenance to 90% from December 1, freeing over ₹40,000 crore
stories.dek: The central bank reverses its October increase after banking system liquidity turned to deficit for the first time in five months.
stories.summary: The Reserve Bank of India has reduced the share of required cash reserves that banks must hold every day, from 99% to 90%, starting with the fortnight beginning December 1. The change is expected to free more than ₹40,000 crore for banks.
body: The Reserve Bank of India on Friday reduced the share of the cash reserve ratio (CRR) that banks must hold with it every day, from 99% to 90%, starting with the fortnight beginning December 1, 2026.
The change leaves banks with more money to lend. More than ₹40,000 crore is expected to move back into the banking system. Treasury officials put the figure at ₹50,000 crore.

CRR is the share of deposits that banks must keep with the RBI. Banks earn no return on it. It is currently 3% of a bank's net demand and time liabilities, which is the money customers hold in current, savings and fixed deposits.

The RBI said it took the decision after "an assessment of the current and evolving macroeconomic situation and liquidity conditions". Banks must now hold at least 90% of the prescribed CRR on each day of the fortnight. The average over the fortnight must still not fall below the prescribed level.

The move reverses a step announced on October 9, when the RBI raised the daily requirement from 90% to 99%, effective from the fortnight beginning October 16. That came when the system had surplus liquidity after large inflows through foreign currency non-resident (FCNR-B) deposits.
Liquidity has since tightened. The banking system moved to a deficit for the first time in five months, on Goods and Services Tax outflows and the RBI's foreign exchange market interventions.

The deficit, measured by what banks borrowed through the RBI's liquidity adjustment facility, was ₹47,641 crore on Thursday. The weighted average call rate, the rate at which banks lend to each other overnight, was near the upper end of the RBI's rate corridor, the marginal standing facility rate of 5.75%. The repo rate is 5.5%.

At the weekly government bond auction, the RBI accepted bids worth ₹3,677.495 crore against a notified ₹9,000 crore in the 6.20% GS 2029, as investors sought higher yields. The 10-year bond yield rose 3 basis points to 7.27%.
The RBI's policy decision is due next week. The central bank is widely expected to raise rates by 25 basis points, though some economists see room for a larger increase.
keyFacts: The RBI's prescribed CRR is currently 3% of banks' net demand and time liabilities.
The daily requirement was raised to 99% from the fortnight beginning October 16.
The banking system liquidity deficit was ₹47,641 crore on Thursday.
The 10-year government bond yield settled at 7.27%, up 3 basis points.
The rupee fell for a second day to 92.99 per dollar.
stories.background: The RBI raised the daily CRR requirement from 90% to 99% on October 9, effective October 16, when the banking system had surplus liquidity partly because of FCNR-B deposit inflows. Since then the surplus has turned to a deficit.
stories.whatNext: The RBI announces its policy decision next week, and the new CRR rule takes effect from the fortnight beginning December 1.

stories.headline: Supreme Court warns states of penalties over Yamuna pollution, orders live data
stories.dek: The National Green Tribunal separately asked the Delhi Jal Board to explain untreated sewage in city drains and ordered spot inspections within four weeks.
stories.summary: The Supreme Court warned states and Union Territories of penalties if they fail to curb Yamuna pollution, and ordered real-time data from treatment plants. The National Green Tribunal separately asked the Delhi Jal Board to explain sewage still flowing into Delhi drains.
body: The Supreme Court has warned states and Union Territories that they face penalties if they fail to control pollution in the Yamuna, whether the cause is poor performance or weak political commitment.

The river passes through several states and Delhi, and major drains empty into it. Its quality at state borders is currently checked only once every three months. The court's directions aim to make each jurisdiction answerable for the water it passes on.

In its November 4 order, Justices Manoj Misra and Manmohan said the court was neither a city planner nor an expert body. They said civic authorities must prepare a comprehensive plan rather than rely only on more sewage treatment plants (STPs), decentralised treatment units and biogas plants.

The Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) must submit water quality data, including biochemical oxygen demand, chemical oxygen demand, faecal coliform and total suspended solids. The data must cover points where the Yamuna and major drains enter and leave each state, Union Territory and district. The board must also investigate fish deaths, white foam and algal blooms and recommend remedies.

Existing STPs, common effluent treatment plants and government-commissioned biogas plants must fit tamper-proof smart energy meters within one month. STPs and effluent plants must also install flow meters with continuous sensors and test faecal coliform levels weekly in accredited laboratories. All readings must be uploaded in real time.

A gap in data transmission of more than 24 hours will be treated as evidence that a plant is not running, unless the operator proves otherwise. The Delhi Pollution Control Committee (DPCC) told the court it is installing real-time monitoring stations on the Yamuna and major drains. Other state pollution control bodies must do the same and share data with the CPCB.

In a separate order on November 17, reviewing the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026, the court noted that 4,592 interception systems had been installed and 21,324.69 tonnes of waste removed from riverbanks and water bodies. Restoration work on 778 river stretches was under way or substantially complete. About 400 districts have yet to set up special monitoring cells, and only nine of 28 states have met the urban bye-law target.

The National Green Tribunal (NGT), in an order dated November 25, asked the Delhi Jal Board (DJB) to explain why untreated sewage still flows into city drains. Advocates showed photographs they said showed sewage entering Drain No. 22 (Pant Nagar/Lajpat Nagar), though the board had reported trapping work there as complete.

The tribunal, headed by Justice Prakash Shrivastava, said legal action may follow if the DJB chief engineer's affidavit of November 21 is found to be incorrect. It directed the DPCC to inspect the sites, take samples and report within four weeks. The DJB has two weeks to file an affidavit on STP progress, delays and revised timelines, and to say whether a nano-bubbles plant near Defence Colony works. A DJB official said the agency will state its position before the tribunal.
The Supreme Court has asked District Collectors to upload geotagged photographs of waste facilities, with progress updates due as of January 1, 2027.
keyFacts: The Supreme Court's Yamuna order is dated November 4, 2026.
Data gaps beyond 24 hours will be treated as proof a plant is not operating.
The NGT gave the DPCC four weeks to report on spot inspections.
The DJB has two weeks to file a further affidavit on STP and DSTP projects.
Several of 22 identified drain projects have been pushed to March or June 2027.
stories.background: The Yamuna flows through Uttarakhand, Himachal Pradesh, Haryana, Delhi and Uttar Pradesh. The CPCB is the national pollution regulator, the DPCC its Delhi counterpart, and the DJB runs Delhi's water and sewage services. The NGT is hearing the Nizamuddin West Association case against the Union of India on drain pollution.

stories.headline: Film workers' body threatens to pull crews from Netflix shoots over Pakistani series
stories.dek: The Federation of Western India Cine Employees says it will stop work on Netflix productions if 'Jo Bachay Hain Sang Samait Lo' is released; the series is due to premiere on December 4.
stories.summary: The Federation of Western India Cine Employees has threatened to withdraw its members from Netflix shoots across India if the Pakistani series 'Jo Bachay Hain Sang Samait Lo' is released. The I&B ministry has asked Netflix to follow its 2025 advisory on Pakistani content.
body: The Federation of Western India Cine Employees (FWICE) has threatened to pull its workers off Netflix productions across India if the platform releases the Pakistani series 'Jo Bachay Hain Sang Samait Lo'.

The warning affects crews, technicians and artists on Netflix projects in India. The series, described as Netflix's first Pakistani original, is due to premiere on December 4. Its cast includes Fawad Khan, Mahira Khan, Sanam Saeed, Hania Aamir and Ahad Raza Mir.

FWICE president BN Tiwari issued the warning on Thursday. He told the news agency ANI: "If they do not stop this, then wherever their shooting is taking place, I will pull our people out from there, and their shooting at every location will be stopped."

Tiwari said the government had told streaming platforms last year not to show Pakistani content. He claimed Netflix had assured the government it would not stream material against India's policies or national interests. He also said FWICE represents almost 95% of workers, technicians and artists in the industry, with nearly five lakh members in western India.

Filmmaker Ashoke Pandit, president of the Indian Film & Television Directors' Association, backed the stand. He told ANI that FWICE would issue a non-cooperation directive if Netflix India failed to respect "our national sentiments". Under it, he said, none of the federation's workers or technicians would work on Netflix productions. He also asked why others in Bollywood were not speaking up.

The Ministry of Information and Broadcasting on Thursday asked Netflix to stick to its 2025 advisory on Pakistani content. It also asked the platform to maintain what it told the government in June last year: that it had not made any Pakistan-origin film or series available to Indian subscribers.

The advisory dates to May 8, 2025, after the April 22 Pahalgam attack, which killed 25 Indians and one Nepalese citizen. The ministry told streaming platforms to remove Pakistan-origin content. It cited the IT (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules, 2021, which bar content that threatens India's unity, security, sovereignty, friendly relations with foreign states or public order.
The All Indian Cine Workers Association has also sought a continued ban. FWICE has written to Prime Minister Narendra Modi asking him to stop the release in India.

Tiwari said Netflix's control was from America. He said that otherwise, "if it had been from any corner of India, we would have stopped it by now". Netflix has not said whether Indian subscribers will get the series, and its response to the federation's warning was not available.

The series is based on Farhat Ishtiaq's 2013 Urdu novel of the same name and follows six love stories. It is created, directed and produced by Momina Duraid. Its trailer was unveiled at Karachi's Mohatta Palace.

Film bodies have since pressed for the ban to continue. The AICWA says it barred Pakistani artistes from working in India after the 2019 Pulwama attack.

stories.headline: Karnataka bars three IOCL fuel meters at Bengaluru terminal over measurement gaps
stories.dek: The state's Legal Metrology Department gave Indian Oil seven days to explain why its meters at Devanagonthi recorded excess ethanol and short deliveries of petrol.
stories.summary: Karnataka's Legal Metrology Department has barred three Indian Oil meters at its Devanagonthi terminal from commercial use after finding errors in ethanol and petrol readings. It issued a show-cause notice giving the company seven days to respond.
body: Karnataka's Legal Metrology Department has barred three fuel measurement systems at an Indian Oil Corporation Limited (IOCL) terminal at Devanagonthi near Bengaluru from commercial use, after finding errors in ethanol and petrol readings.
The meters measure fuel that oil marketing companies supply to petrol stations and dealers. The notice said wrong readings could affect the interests of consumers, dealers and other stakeholders.

The show-cause notice is dated November 25, the day of the inspection. It was issued by the Joint Controller of Legal Metrology, Bangalore and Mysore Division, to the Deputy General Manager in charge of the terminal. A show-cause notice asks a party to explain why action should not be taken against it.

Officials tested the three mass flow meters against a verified master proving measure. An ethanol meter at Bay No. 9 delivered 14 litres too much for every 3,000 litres. A motor gasoline meter at the same bay delivered four to six litres too little for every 3,000 litres. An ethanol meter at Bay No. 4 delivered three litres too much.

Rizwan Arshad, Karnataka's minister for food, civil supplies, consumer affairs and legal metrology, said all the discrepancies were beyond permissible limits. "After the Karnataka government exposed over-blending of ethanol in petrol beyond the prescribed E20 limit, our Legal Metrology Department has begun inspecting Oil Marketing Company (OMC) terminals, where the blending is carried out," he said.

IOCL has seven days from receiving the notice to submit verification certificates, calibration and maintenance records, and an account of steps taken to ensure the meters and their batch control units are accurate. It must also propose corrective measures.

The notice also asks why legal and departmental action should not be taken against the terminal and the people who operate and maintain the equipment. It says an unsatisfactory reply could lead to further proceedings under the Legal Metrology Act, 2009, without another notice. IOCL had not commented when the story was published.

The inspection follows an earlier dispute over ethanol in petrol. The state collected 63 petrol samples from retail outlets in seven districts. Of 14 results initially available, 11 showed ethanol above the 20% limit, with a high of 31.2% at an IOCL outlet.
IOCL, Bharat Petroleum and Hindustan Petroleum questioned the state's sampling and testing. They said their own tests of 56 samples in Karnataka found ethanol between 19% and 20%.

stories.headline: EC revises Bengal roll revision schedule; final rolls to come out on February 8
stories.dek: The draft roll will now be published on December 15, and the commission has issued rules for voters still marked 'Under Adjudication' in the earlier intensive revision.
stories.summary: The Election Commission has set a new timetable for the Special Summary Revision in West Bengal, with the draft roll on December 15 and the final roll on February 8. It also issued instructions on voters still 'Under Adjudication'.
body: The Election Commission of India on Friday announced a revised schedule for the Special Summary Revision of electoral rolls in West Bengal, with the final roll to be published on February 8.

The revision decides who can vote in the state. Voters who were left out, and young people turning 18 by January 1, 2027, are being urged to check their details and apply for enrolment or corrections.
Polling stations will be rationalised and rearranged by December 3. The integrated draft roll will come out on December 15. The qualifying date remains January 1, 2027.
Voters can file claims and objections between December 15 and January 14. These are to be settled by February 1.
The draft roll was earlier due on November 23. The commission postponed it on November 20, citing "unavoidable circumstances". The earlier schedule had put the final roll on January 16, 2027.

The state Chief Electoral Officer's office has announced special campaign days in December and January. In December they fall on the 19th, 20th, 26th and 27th. In January they are on the 2nd, 3rd, 9th and 10th.

Booth Level Officers will be at designated polling stations on those days to help voters with enrolment, corrections, claims and objections. A senior official said representatives of registered parties have also been asked to attend.

The commission also wrote to the Chief Electoral Officer on voters still marked 'Under Adjudication' in the Special Intensive Revision, the earlier and more detailed exercise. If a Judicial Officer has passed an order but not e-signed it, the case will be treated as decided, and the Electoral Registration Officer will update the roll accordingly. Cases not yet adjudicated will go to the Electoral Registration Officers for decisions.

No action will be taken for voters whose names were deleted and who did not appeal. For deleted voters with appeals pending, the Supreme Court's directions of November 23 on prioritising appeals must be followed. "If these persons file Form 6 for fresh inclusion, EROs should not process it until the Appellate Tribunal decides the appeal," the letter said.

The commission also revised the monthly honorarium for Appellate Tribunal judges. A former High Court Chief Justice will get ₹2,60,000, and other former High Court judges ₹2,50,000. More than 37 lakh cases are pending in the 19 appellate tribunals.
keyFacts: Polling stations in Bengal are to be rationalised by December 3.
Claims and objections are to be disposed of by February 1, 2027.
Special campaign days include December 19, 20, 26 and 27, and January 2, 3, 9 and 10.

stories.background: The story so far: On October 15 the commission issued a revision schedule for 14 states and three Union Territories, including Bengal, with a draft roll due on November 12 and a final roll on January 4. On October 28 it moved the Bengal draft roll to November 23. On November 20 it postponed that date, citing "unavoidable circumstances". On Friday it set December 15 for the draft and February 8 for the final roll.

stories.headline: CERT-In warns of high-severity flaws in WhatsApp and critical ones in ASUS software
stories.dek: The government's cyber agency issued two separate advisories and asked users and organisations to install the fixes released by WhatsApp and ASUS.
stories.summary: India's cyber agency CERT-In has flagged high-severity flaws in WhatsApp and WhatsApp Business and critical flaws in ASUS management software. It asked users to install the updates the companies have released.
body: The Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) has warned of high-severity security flaws in WhatsApp and critical flaws in ASUS software, and asked users to update.

WhatsApp has a very large user base in India, and the ASUS software is used to manage computers and company systems. The flaws could let attackers run malicious code or take administrator control of a system.

In advisory CIVN-2026-0576, CERT-In said the WhatsApp flaws affect WhatsApp and WhatsApp Business on Android and iOS, and the apps for Mac and Windows. It listed their causes as attachment spoofing, SQL injection, improper certificate chain validation, and incomplete checks of AI rich response messages and external ad-reply URLs.

The agency said a remote attacker could send a specially crafted message, attachment or URL to a device. This could allow code to run, expose sensitive information, bypass security restrictions or change app data.

WhatsApp's owner, Meta, has fixed the flaws in its latest versions and published details on its website. It said it has found no sign that four of the five flaws were used by anyone. It has not ruled out that the flaw involving ads that open a chat with a business, which could reveal a user's IP address, was exploited along with spam messages.

CERT-In rated the risk 'High' and asked users to update through the Google Play Store, the App Store or the Microsoft Store. Fixed versions include WhatsApp for Android 2.26.35.74 and WhatsApp for iOS 2.26.24.72.

In a separate advisory, CIVN-2026-0575, CERT-In rated flaws in ASUS software 'critical'. The affected products are ASUS Control Center Express, Control Center Datacenter, Control Center Enterprise and Armoury Crate.

The agency said the flaws come from hard-coded cryptographic keys, missing or incorrect authorisation checks, and an untrusted search path. An attacker could forge authentication tokens, create administrator accounts, change administrator passwords or run malicious libraries with elevated privileges.

CERT-In asked users and organisations to install the updates listed in ASUS's security advisories. Affected versions are Control Center Express before 1.7.29, Datacenter 4.0.0.2 and earlier, Enterprise 3.1.0.8 and earlier, and Armoury Crate up to and including 6.7.2.
keyFacts: CERT-In advisory CIVN-2026-0576 covers WhatsApp; CIVN-2026-0575 covers ASUS software.
The WhatsApp advisory is rated high risk; the ASUS advisory is rated critical.
WhatsApp for Windows is affected in versions before 2.3000.1032164386.258709.
ASUS Armoury Crate is affected up to and including version 6.7.2.

stories.background: CERT-In is the government's nodal agency for responding to cyber security incidents and works under the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology. It issues advisories when flaws are reported in software used in India. It has flagged WhatsApp flaws before, in 2019, 2021 and 2025.

stories.headline: Zelensky calls Trump's 'friend' remark about Putin strange, warns of new Russian strike
stories.dek: Ukraine's president urged the US to press Moscow harder, as Kyiv put forward a Black Sea ceasefire plan to protect its grain exports.
stories.summary: Volodymyr Zelensky told the BBC it was "strange" for Donald Trump to call Vladimir Putin a friend, and said Russia was preparing a new mass strike. Kyiv also proposed a Black Sea ceasefire to protect grain exports.
body: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said on Friday that it was "strange" for US President Donald Trump to call Russian President Vladimir Putin "my friend", in an interview with the BBC in Kyiv.

The remarks matter because Washington is mediating peace talks, and Kyiv says delays in US weapons deliveries and a lack of pressure on Moscow are costing Ukrainian lives. Russian strikes are hitting power stations and bridges ahead of winter.

"He's an aggressor, and a killer... He can't be a friend. Just cannot be," Zelensky said, speaking in English. He compared it to someone calling Adolf Hitler a friend during World War Two. He also said: "When you try to be very neutral with the aggressor... it means you support victims and you support also aggressor. It's not right."

Asked about the remark on Thursday, Trump told reporters: "We want to stop killing. I could say he's not a friend... I want to make a deal." He said the biggest problem to a settlement was that "you have two leaders that really hate each other". The US says it is neutral in the search for a deal that can hold.

Trump posted on Truth Social that he urged Putin at their summit in China last week to "pull back all military aggression against territories throughout Europe". He said a peace deal was "a strong possibility".
Zelensky said the latest talks in Abu Dhabi this month made little progress and were expected to resume in December. He said it was not clear whether European negotiators would be at the table.

On Thursday, in his nightly video address, Zelensky said Ukraine had information that Russia was preparing a new mass strike. He asked people to heed missile alerts in the coming days. It was his second such warning this week.

Zelensky said there is a "very, very big" shortage of interceptors against ballistic missiles and that the US was delaying Patriot deliveries. He said Ukraine can now destroy about 70% of Russia's fastest drones.

Separately, Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha said on Friday that Ukraine had presented a proposal for a Black Sea ceasefire, to restore freedom of navigation and allow uninterrupted farm exports. "We are now awaiting a response from Russia," he said.
Sybiha said Moscow wanted oil transport included, while Ukraine says that belongs in a wider energy ceasefire. He accused Russia of making "unrealistic demands".
keyFacts: Zelensky said Ukraine can destroy about 70% of Russia's fastest drones, a figure he said is improving.
Kyiv mayor Vitali Klitschko said seven people were wounded in an overnight ballistic missile attack on Kyiv.
Zelensky defended the sinking of the Russian warship Merkury off Libya as an "absolutely fair goal".
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on October 31 Washington was reviewing Turkiye and India proposals on grain and energy shipments.
stories.background: Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022. A UN- and Turkiye-brokered grain deal let Ukrainian exports resume, but Moscow withdrew in July 2023. Zelensky has been wary with Washington since a tense Oval Office meeting with Trump in 2025. US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff are mediating. Talks in Abu Dhabi this month made little progress. Trump met Putin in China last week.
stories.whatNext: Peace talks are expected to resume in December, and Ukraine is awaiting Russia's reply on the Black Sea proposal.

stories.headline: Hackers breach US Air Force's Cloud One computing platform, Reuters reports
stories.dek: The intrusion, found during a system upgrade, has paused work and blocked software updates on a platform that supports missile-tracking and air defence data systems.
stories.summary: Hackers have broken into the US Air Force's Cloud One cloud computing platform, three people familiar with the matter told Reuters. The Air Force declined to comment on the status of specific systems, and the hackers' identity and the scale of the intrusion are not known.
body: Hackers have breached the US Air Force's flagship cloud computing platform, Cloud One, three people familiar with the matter told Reuters on Friday.

The platform holds sensitive personnel, logistics and tactical data and supports systems that track bombs and missiles. The identity of the hackers, the full scope of the intrusion and whether any data was stolen have not been established.
Two of the people said the intrusion was found within the past month or so during work to upgrade the system. They said the discovery led to disruption across the platform.

Efforts to move back-office applications onto Cloud One, a longstanding military priority, have been paused, according to two of the sources and a fourth person. Updates to applications already running on it were blocked, so Air Force staff could not apply fixes just as a new batch of serious software flaws was disclosed across the technology industry. A fifth source said some users had their administrator rights revoked.

One source said the intruders used a software vulnerability to reach the platform's control plane. The source compared it to a universal remote. In theory, access could allow someone to check the operational status of military aircraft or the movement of spare parts. It is unclear whether the hackers did so.

The Air Force said in a statement that it "does not comment on the security posture, vulnerabilities or operational status of specific networks and systems." It added: "We continuously take prudent measures to protect Department (of the Air Force) information, systems and mission capabilities."

One source said investigators have called in Cyber Command, the US military's cyber force, to assess the damage. Cyber Command did not respond to requests for comment. "A breach here is a big deal," one source said.

Cloud One began in 2017 as a single hub for Air Force IT needs. It combines services from Microsoft, Amazon, Oracle and Alphabet. Among its applications are the Cloud-Based Command and Control system, which collates air defence radar and other data from across North America, and the Theater Integrated Combat Munitions System, which tracks munitions at more than 200 Air Force locations worldwide.
SAIC was the prime contractor until 2025, when Leidos took over. SAIC did not respond to a request for comment, and Leidos referred questions to the Air Force.

The US government is also handling the aftermath of at least six other cyber incidents disclosed recently. These include two at the FBI, an earlier theft of Pentagon data, an exposure of Department of Homeland Security staff details, an intrusion into two intelligence agencies and an attack on the Treasury Department.

In a 2023 commentary, Cloud One's leadership claimed a "100% success rate" against intrusion attempts.

No link between them and Cloud One has been confirmed.

stories.headline: Houthi media say Saudi strike on Yemen's Taiz killed 11, most of them children
stories.dek: The Saudi-led coalition said separately it shot down a drone aimed at Riyadh, a day after a Houthi attack shut the Jazan refinery.
stories.summary: Houthi media said a Saudi air raid on a residential building in Al-Turba, Taiz, killed 11 people on Friday, most of them children. Saudi authorities have reported 27 deaths from Houthi attacks in the kingdom since the war reignited.
body: A Saudi air raid on a residential building in the city of Al-Turba in Yemen's Taiz governorate killed 11 people, most of them children, on Friday, the Houthis' Saba news agency reported.

The report adds to the toll of a war that restarted in July and has drawn in Saudi cities, including Riyadh. Neither the Saudi government nor the coalition it leads had commented on the Al-Turba claim in the material available. The figure has not been independently verified.
Saba cited a local source. It also reported strikes on fuel tanks in Saada, the Houthi movement's birthplace and stronghold.
The Saudi-led coalition, which backs Yemen's internationally recognised government, said on Friday that it shot down a drone targeting Riyadh.

On Thursday, the Houthis attacked the Jazan refinery in southern Saudi Arabia, the Saudi Press Agency said. A Nepalese worker was killed and several people were hurt. A fire shut the facility, the agency said.

Earlier on Thursday, Anees al-Asbahi, a spokesperson for the Houthi-run health ministry, said strikes across Taiz province killed four people, including a child. He blamed Saudi Arabia. Al-Masirah, the Houthi-controlled television channel, reported strikes on Sanaa overnight, and two residents told the Associated Press they heard explosions in the capital. The AP could not independently verify the Houthi claims.
Since fighting resumed, the United Nations says more than 2,300 people have been killed in Yemen and over 364,000 displaced. Saudi authorities say Houthi attacks in the kingdom have killed 27 people.

The Houthis say their attacks on Saudi Arabia are retaliation for Saudi air strikes in Yemen and for what they call a Saudi blockade of ports and airports in areas they hold. The Saudi government has condemned what it calls terrorist attacks on civilian and economic facilities. It has said it will take all necessary measures to defend itself.
keyFacts: Saba reported the Al-Turba raid hit a residential building in Taiz governorate on Friday.
The Jazan refinery was shut by fire after a Houthi attack on Thursday.
The UN says over 2,300 people have been killed in Yemen since July.
Saudi authorities say Houthi attacks in the kingdom have killed 27 people.
The Houthis are advancing toward Aden, where the government has taken refuge.
stories.background: Yemen's informal ceasefire unravelled in July after years of relative calm. Fighting intensified in September, when the Houthis, who already held the most densely populated areas, seized the western coastline overlooking the Bab el-Mandeb strait. The Houthis have since struck Saudi airports, oil sites and Riyadh's financial district. The Saudi-led coalition has bombed Houthi-held areas.

stories.headline: Delhi government opens Kejriwal's former residence to media, with price tags on fittings
stories.dek: PWD Minister Parvesh Verma led the tour of 6 Flagstaff Road and said it would open to the public next month; AAP called it a diversion.
stories.summary: The BJP-led Delhi government showed journalists Arvind Kejriwal's former official residence on Friday, with a price tag on each item. The AAP said the exercise was meant to divert attention from pollution in the Yamuna.
body: The Delhi government on Friday opened 6 Flagstaff Road, the bungalow where former chief minister Arvind Kejriwal lived from 2015 to October 2024, to the media, with prices displayed beside furniture and fittings.

The bungalow, which the BJP calls 'Sheesh Mahal', has been at the centre of a long political fight over the cost of its renovation. The tour comes before plans to open it to the public next month, and ahead of next year's Punjab Assembly election, in which the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) is seeking another term.

Public Works Department (PWD) officials said a baithak with a sliding door was listed at Rs 41.16 lakh, a powder room at Rs 5.80 lakh and the lobby area at Rs 7.58 lakh. Chandeliers above a 14-seat dining table were priced at around Rs 11 lakh. Other items shown included a Rs 5.47-lakh two-seater sofa and a Rs 2.42-lakh recliner.

The house covers 1,905 square metres and has eight bedrooms, 13 bathrooms and a wellness room with a sauna and jacuzzi. Boards at the entrance read "Welcome to Sheesh Mahal, built at a cost of Rs 58 crore". A red carpet was laid inside.

PWD Minister Parvesh Verma led the tour. "We have only one objective: every government should provide a full account of where and how much of Delhi residents' money, that is, taxpayers' money, has been spent," he told reporters. "We have no political motive here." He said each amount came with a bill and invoice number, and that the house was "exactly as it was before".

Chief Minister Rekha Gupta urged people in Delhi and Punjab to visit. She said AAP had "looted" Delhi and was now "looting" Punjab. Delhi minister Kapil Mishra said the public across the country would be able to see the house through the media's cameras.

AAP rejected the exercise. Delhi unit president Saurabh Bharadwaj said the government was using it to divert attention from pollution in the Yamuna, including the deaths of thousands of fish. He asked Verma to answer questions about the river. The Hindu reported that AAP did not comment on the issue to it.

A report by the Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG), tabled in the Delhi Assembly in March 2026, put the renovation cost at Rs 33.66 crore, against an estimate of Rs 7.91 crore. The Rs 58 crore figure on the boards is the BJP's claim. Central investigative agencies are examining the alleged irregularities, and AAP has denied them.

Officials said public entry would be through online booking, with a ticket likely to cost around Rs 20. Senior citizens and college students would enter free. The government has said it plans to bring in a private hospitality firm to manage the residence for official conferences, lunches and meetings.

stories.headline: SAP preparing to cut at least 10,000 jobs as it shifts to AI, Bloomberg reports
stories.dek: The German software maker did not confirm a number, saying no decisions had been made. Separately, it said it found no evidence that customer business data was accessed in a security incident.
stories.summary: SAP is preparing a plan to cut at least 10,000 jobs as it reshapes its business around artificial intelligence, Bloomberg reported. The company said no decisions had been made, and separately reported a security incident without evidence of customer data access.
body: SAP, the German business software maker, is preparing a plan to eliminate at least 10,000 positions as it reshapes its business around artificial intelligence, Bloomberg reported on Thursday, citing people familiar with the matter.

SAP sells software that companies use to run finance, human resources, procurement and supply chains. It employs more than 110,000 people worldwide, so the reported cuts would affect roughly one in eleven of its staff.

In a statement, SAP did not confirm the figure. "The business environment in which we operate is changing rapidly through AI, and we are continuously reviewing how our organization and workforce need to evolve to remain successful," the company said. It added that no decisions had been made on further measures and that it does not comment on speculation.
Bloomberg reported that all departments had been asked to identify possible cuts, with product, engineering and sales under particular focus.

The report came as SAP confirmed a security incident. The company told Reuters it had "identified suspicious activity" and had taken steps to protect its customers and services. "Based on our investigation to date, we have found no evidence of unauthorized access to customer business data," it said.

German magazine Der Spiegel reported that attackers had targeted SAP's presence on GitHub, a platform where developers store and share code. It said they had obtained authentication tokens, which are digital credentials that can give access to accounts and development tools. SAP has not confirmed this. It has not said what the activity was, which systems were affected or who was responsible.

Handelsblatt reported that SAP restricted access to GitHub, suspended automated software-development processes and replaced signing keys, which are used to verify software. It said several teams were affected.

SAP carried out a restructuring in 2024 that removed around 10,000 positions, mainly through voluntary departures and retraining. Headcount then stayed relatively flat as the company hired for new roles, Bloomberg reported.

Chief executive Christian Klein is steering SAP towards what the company describes as an AI-first strategy. This year SAP completed four acquisitions: Reltio, Dremio, Prior Labs and TechWolf. It also invested in Parloa, n8n and Conduct.
Other software firms have linked job cuts to AI. Atlassian said in March it would cut about 1,600 jobs, and Cloudflare said in May it would cut more than 1,100 roles.
keyFacts: SAP employs more than 110,000 people worldwide.

stories.background: SAP, based in Walldorf, is the world's largest vendor of enterprise software, founded in 1972. Klein became a public face of its AI plans; in 2023 he told CNBC he did not necessarily expect the workforce to shrink and expected revenue to grow.

stories.headline: US regulator approves SpaceX plan for up to 1 million data-centre satellites
stories.dek: The American Astronomical Society said it was "disheartened and dismayed" by the Federal Communications Commission's licence for the Starmind constellation, citing risks to astronomy.
stories.summary: The US Federal Communications Commission has licensed SpaceX to deploy up to 1 million Starmind satellites in low Earth orbit to host AI computing. The American Astronomical Society said the plan threatens astronomy and the night sky.
body: The US Federal Communications Commission (FCC) on Wednesday approved SpaceX's plan to put up to 1 million satellites in low Earth orbit to act as data centres for artificial intelligence.

The project, called Starmind, is meant to move some of the electricity-hungry computing that AI needs off the ground. Astronomers and space-safety experts say the scale of the plan could change how the night sky looks and how research is done.
Under the licence, SpaceX must begin deployment by November 2033. It must put up 10 per cent of the maximum, or 100,000 satellites, by November 2035 and 50 per cent by November 2038, the FCC said.
The FCC said the approval would "support America's booming super intelligence economy". Its chair, Brendan Carr, said: "America is leading the world into the era of super intelligence."

SpaceX told the commission that the satellites would draw on "near-constant solar power" with little operating or maintenance cost. It said this would cut the environmental impact of data centres on Earth. Supporters of the idea say such centres could ease the demand for land, electricity and water.

The American Astronomical Society said the constellation "would significantly undermine decades of federal investment in astronomical facilities". It cited bright, reflective satellites, radio interference, pollution from launches and re-entries, and greater collision risk. The European Southern Observatory has called for international mechanisms to assess projects whose effects cross borders.

Amazon's satellite unit, Leo, and others have questioned whether SpaceX will deploy all the satellites. Carr rejected that criticism, saying SpaceX was already launching at a pace its competitors should try to match. SpaceX sought approval for 42,000 Starlink satellites but operates just over 11,000.
The FCC put off a SpaceX request to dispose of satellites above 600 km in so-called graveyard orbits. About 17,000 satellites currently exist.

A July report by the US Government Accountability Office said space data centres could reduce the land, electricity and water used on Earth. It also warned of "engineering and economic barriers", including cooling hardware in space. A Columbia University paper this month said 10 per cent of the AI data centres expected by 2030 would need more than 700 large-rocket launches a year.
keyFacts: The FCC approved the Starmind licence on Wednesday, November 25.
SpaceX must deploy 50 per cent of the satellites by November 2038.
About 17,000 satellites currently exist, according to the FCC.
SpaceX sought approval for 42,000 Starlink satellites but operates just over 11,000.
The FCC deferred SpaceX's request on disposal of satellites above 600 km.
stories.background: Starmind differs from Starlink, SpaceX's internet satellite network, because its satellites would carry computing hardware and process data in orbit. The plan depends on Starship, SpaceX's reusable rocket. Other firms, including Google and Starcloud, are also working on orbital computing.
stories.whatNext: SpaceX must have deployment under way by November 2033 and 100,000 satellites in orbit by November 2035.

stories.headline: High Court issues notice to Satyendar Jain on ACB plea to cancel his bail
stories.dek: Justice Sachin Datta listed the Anti-Corruption Branch's challenge to the September 3 trial court order for hearing on December 22.
stories.summary: The Delhi High Court on Friday asked AAP leader Satyendar Jain to respond to the Anti-Corruption Branch's plea to cancel his bail in the Delhi Jal Board tender case. The matter will be heard next on December 22.
body: The Delhi High Court on Friday issued notice to Aam Aadmi Party leader Satyendar Jain on a plea by the Delhi Police's Anti-Corruption Branch (ACB) to cancel his bail in the Delhi Jal Board corruption case.

The case concerns tenders for upgrading the board's sewage treatment plants, which are public works funded by the government. Justice Sachin Datta sought Jain's response and listed the matter for December 22.

Jain, a former Delhi minister in charge of water, was arrested by the ACB on August 18 and sent to judicial custody the next day. A special judge at the Rouse Avenue Courts, Dig Vinay Singh, granted him bail on September 3.

In that order, the judge questioned the timing of the arrest. He noted a 27-month gap between the registration of the case and the arrest, and said the ACB had not pointed to any new circumstances that warranted it. He also said that, at this stage, none of the WhatsApp chats linked Jain to the other accused, and that no call records or messages connected him to the alleged kickbacks and hawala transactions.

In its plea, the ACB argues that the trial court overlooked that the prosecution has assigned different roles to different accused within one alleged conspiracy. It says the case relies on Jain's approvals or decisions at the policy and administrative stages.

The ACB also says the trial court gave too much weight to the lack of a direct money trail to Jain's personal bank account. It argues the offence is a grave economic offence affecting public funds and infrastructure, and it cites the possibility of Jain influencing witnesses.

The plea states that the trial court "failed to consider that the prosecution case is based upon a coordinated conspiracy" in which officials, a private technology provider and intermediaries allegedly played complementary roles. It adds that direct evidence of every conversation or payment involving the principal accused cannot be insisted upon at the bail stage.

The plea also points out that the trial court itself observed that certain decisions by Jain "raise eyebrows" and that he "may not be innocent", yet granted bail. The ACB was represented by Senior Advocate Sanjeev Bhandari and Additional Standing Counsel Amol Sinha.

The case was registered on May 11, 2024, on a complaint from the Delhi Government's Directorate of Vigilance. It alleges tender conditions were manipulated to favour Euroteck Environment Pvt. Ltd and limit competition. Jain has not been convicted of any offence.
keyFacts: The ACB arrested Satyendar Jain on August 18; he was sent to judicial custody on August 19.

The Enforcement Directorate has separately filed a chargesheet against Jain and 13 others, alleging fraud of Rs 17.7 crore.
The FIR invokes the Prevention of Corruption Act and Indian Penal Code sections including 120B.
stories.background: The ACB alleges that tender conditions for upgrading Delhi Jal Board sewage treatment plants were framed to favour one firm, that no pilot project was run, and that key effluent parameters were left out. The Enforcement Directorate is running a parallel money laundering probe. The ACB also arrested former board chief executive Udit Prakash Rai and four others.
stories.whatNext: The High Court will hear the matter on December 22, by which time Jain is to have filed his response.

stories.headline: Israeli judges urge prosecutors to end Netanyahu corruption trial
stories.dek: Attorney general Gali Baharav-Miara must decide whether to accept the recommendation, as Gadi Eisenkot says Likud is stalling talks to form a new government.
stories.summary: The judges in Benjamin Netanyahu's corruption trial asked prosecutors to drop or settle the three cases against him. The attorney general must now decide, while coalition talks to replace his caretaker government remain deadlocked.
body: The judges presiding over Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's corruption trial have asked prosecutors to end the case, leaving Attorney General Gali Baharav-Miara to decide whether to accept.

The decision affects Israel's politics directly. Netanyahu is a caretaker prime minister after the October 27 election, and the trial has shaped the country's politics for years. Settling or dropping all charges would end the threat of jail and clear the legal cloud over his political future.
Netanyahu is charged with bribery, fraud and breach of trust in three overlapping cases. They concern his ties to telecoms owners and other wealthy businessmen. He has pleaded not guilty.

The judges urged prosecutors to drop one case because, in their words, "the chances of a conviction are low". They suggested seeking a plea deal in a second case and reconsidering the third. They said that even if the fraud and breach of trust allegations in that case were proved, it was not clear his alleged conduct amounted to a crime.

Baharav-Miara was summoned to court to hear the statement in person. She has resisted similar judicial pressure before. In 2023 and 2025 the judges urged prosecutors to drop the bribery charges, the most serious Netanyahu faces, but did not suggest ending the whole trial.
Netanyahu says he is the victim of a political witch-hunt. He welcomed the recommendation. "The truth has finally come to light," he said.

Critics see risks. Yael Freidson, legal correspondent for Haaretz, said the judges' position would set "an impossible bar for conviction in corruption cases". Oren Persico of The Seventh Eye said ending the trial would tell powerful people that those who fight hard enough can escape accountability. He also said the judges appeared tired of a case that has run since 2020.

Continuing the trial is not simple either. Even if the current bench acquits, a higher court could hear an appeal with different judges. Netanyahu's testimony alone ran over a year and a half across 98 hearings, and the transcripts exceed 60,000 pages, Freidson said.

Separately, Gadi Eisenkot, leader of the centrist Yashar party, accused Netanyahu's Likud of stalling coalition talks. President-appointed Eisenkot has until December 6 to form a government, and the deadline can be extended by 14 days.

In a statement on Friday, Eisenkot said Likud had refused for two weeks to table a single concrete proposal. He said its conduct pointed to an effort to run down the clock and force another election under the outgoing government. Likud accused him of working to form a "dangerous left-wing government" but said it remained open to a unity government.
Yashar has agreed deals with the Democrats and Israel Beiteinu, giving a combined 36 seats, short of the 61 needed in the 120-seat parliament.

Yashar, Democrats and Israel Beiteinu together hold 36 seats; 61 are needed.
The October 27 election gave Eisenkot's bloc 48 seats and Netanyahu's alliance 53.

stories.background: Netanyahu was indicted in 2019 on bribery, fraud and breach of trust charges, and the trial began in 2020. The October 27 election produced no clear majority for either bloc. Israel's president asked Eisenkot to try to form a government.

stories.headline: Himalayan water bodies begin freezing as IMD warns of dense fog in north, heavy rain in south
stories.dek: Shopian recorded -4.4°C and Tabo -4.2°C, while isolated heavy rain of 64.5-115.5 mm is forecast for Kerala, Tamil Nadu and Puducherry.
stories.summary: The India Meteorological Department has forecast dense fog across Punjab, Haryana and Chandigarh and heavy rain in southern India. Water bodies at higher altitudes in Kashmir and Himachal Pradesh have begun to freeze as night temperatures fall below zero.
body: Temperatures fell below freezing in parts of Kashmir and Himachal Pradesh, and water bodies in higher areas began to freeze, as the India Meteorological Department (IMD) warned of dense fog in the north and heavy rain in the south.

The fog could disrupt road and rail travel in Punjab, Haryana and Chandigarh. Heavy rain and thunderstorms are forecast for Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and nearby areas. In its bulletin of November 27, the IMD said night temperatures across north-western India are falling after a western disturbance, a weather system that brings rain and snow to the region, moved away.
In Kashmir, Shopian recorded the Valley's lowest minimum at -4.4°C. Srinagar recorded -1.9°C for the second night in a row. In Himachal Pradesh, Tabo recorded -4.2°C.

The IMD forecast colder conditions in Uttarakhand on November 27 and 28, with frost likely at isolated places in the hills and plains. It said frost could affect crops. No significant rain is forecast in the state until early December.

Delhi is expected to have foggy mornings and largely clear days. The IMD forecast a minimum of around 10°C and a maximum of 27°C in the capital on Friday. Delhi's coldest reading on November 26 was 9°C. Moderate fog is possible at the Safdarjung station on Saturday and Sunday.

Parts of eastern and western Uttar Pradesh may see fog on November 27 and 28. Parts of eastern Rajasthan could have cold wave-like conditions on those days. Sikar recorded 5°C on November 26, one of the lowest in the plains. Minimum temperatures were also well below normal in parts of Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Jharkhand, Rajasthan, and Saurashtra and Kutch in Gujarat.

In the south, the IMD forecast isolated heavy rainfall of 64.5-115.5 mm across Kerala, Mahe, Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal. Thunderstorms with lightning are likely in parts of Andhra Pradesh, Kerala, Mahe, Lakshadweep, Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal, with gusts of 30 to 40 km/h. Isolated places in Andhra Pradesh may also see strong winds at the surface.

Kayalipatnam in Thoothukudi district, Tamil Nadu, recorded 18 cm of rain in the 24 hours to Thursday morning. Angadippuram in Kerala recorded 10 cm. For Chennai, the IMD forecast light rain on Saturday, with temperatures between 24°C and 31°C. Bengaluru is expected to see partly cloudy skies over the weekend.
The IMD said a fresh upper-air cyclonic circulation could develop over the south Andaman Sea around November 29.

stories.headline: Shivakumar says many striking ASHA workers want to resume work, rules out written assurance
stories.dek: The Karnataka Chief Minister said he would not sign the assurance the protesting workers demand, and asked them to withdraw their agitation in Bengaluru.
stories.summary: Chief Minister D K Shivakumar said on Friday that many ASHA workers had messaged him offering to return to work, but he would not give a written assurance. The strike, now in its 11th day, centres on a demand to raise the monthly honorarium.
body: Karnataka Chief Minister D K Shivakumar said on Friday that many ASHA workers had contacted him about resuming work, while ruling out the written assurance the protesting workers want.

The strike by ASHAs, the community health workers who link villages and urban neighbourhoods to public health services, entered its 11th day on Friday at Freedom Park in Bengaluru. The workers want their monthly honorarium raised from ₹8,000 to ₹15,000, along with better service benefits.

Speaking to reporters near the BGS grounds in Kengeri, Shivakumar said many workers had messaged him to say they had faith in the government. He said he would not make the messages public, to avoid creating divisions among them.

"You came forward to serve people, not to protest," he said. "If you insist that I sign an assurance, that is not possible." He appealed to them to withdraw the protest and said the government would discuss their demands and decide after consulting all stakeholders.

Shivakumar also turned on leaders of the National Democratic Alliance (NDA) who have commented on the strike. He said the Centre had not raised its contribution to ASHA remuneration by even Re 1, and that the state government had increased the pay. He said neither H D Kumaraswamy nor BJP leaders had spoken about this.

He said the Congress government would keep its manifesto promise to raise the workers' remuneration. "We made a promise in our manifesto, and we will walk the talk," he said, adding that the NDA should press the Centre to increase its share. He called the workers his sisters and said the government had no intention of politicising the issue.
Former chief minister Siddaramaiah, asked about the protest, said it was not his government now. "It is D K Shivakumar who is the head of the government. I presume he'll sort it out," he said.

The union's vice-president, Uma Devi, has criticised Health Minister U T Khader's assertion that the state's health system can function without ASHAs. The BJP has also criticised Khader and appealed to the Governor to intervene.

The workers also protested in August and December 2025.

stories.dek: Karnataka Deputy Chief Minister G. Parameshwara called the state's voice in Parliament a serious concern, while Union Minister H.D. Kumaraswamy said his party would back the Bill.
stories.summary: Former Karnataka Chief Minister Siddaramaiah demanded an all-party meeting on the Centre's delimitation plan and asked the Prime Minister to explain the proposed 50% rise in Lok Sabha seats. JD(S) said it would support the Bill.
body: Former Karnataka Chief Minister Siddaramaiah on Friday demanded that the Prime Minister convene an all-party meeting on the Union Cabinet's delimitation proposal and explain the reasoning behind a 50% increase in Lok Sabha seats.

Delimitation is the redrawing of constituency boundaries and the reallocation of seats. Karnataka and other southern states, which have slowed population growth, fear a loss of influence in Parliament.
The Union Cabinet, chaired by Narendra Modi, has cleared a fresh delimitation Bill. It is expected to be introduced in a special sitting of Parliament beginning on November 30.
In a post on X, Siddaramaiah said Karnataka's seats would rise from 28 to 42 and Uttar Pradesh's from 80 to 120. "The numerical gap will widen from 52 to 78 seats," he said.

He asked the Prime Minister to publish the rationale for the expansion and to place alternative delimitation models before the country. "Karnataka seeks neither special privileges nor representation at the expense of another State," he said.
Siddaramaiah also called on BJP MPs from Karnataka to oppose any framework that does not ensure fair representation for the state. He said they "must stop being mere yes-men to Narendra Modi".

On women's reservation, he said the Congress-led UPA government introduced the Bill in 2008 and passed it in the Rajya Sabha in 2010. He said the Modi government linked its implementation to the Census and delimitation in 2023. He asked why women should wait for Parliament to expand, and said the BJP could implement the reservation within the existing strength of the Lok Sabha and state assemblies.

Deputy Chief Minister G. Parameshwara, also on X, said Karnataka's political representation and voice in Parliament were a matter of serious concern. "More seats alone do not translate into greater political influence," he said. He and Siddaramaiah both said they did not oppose women's reservation and wanted it implemented in the existing 543-seat Lok Sabha.

Union Minister H.D. Kumaraswamy said the Janata Dal (Secular) would support the Bill. He said there would be more Kannadigas in the Lok Sabha after delimitation and that the state's interests would not be hampered.

An earlier Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, introduced in April with a delimitation Bill, failed in the Lok Sabha. It received 298 votes in favour and 230 against, short of the two-thirds majority required.
keyFacts: The special sitting of Parliament begins on November 30.
Karnataka would go from 28 to 42 Lok Sabha seats under a 50% rise, Siddaramaiah said.
The April amendment Bill drew 298 votes for and 230 against in the Lok Sabha.
The earlier Bill proposed raising Lok Sabha seats from 543 to 850.
JD(S) has said it will support the new Bill.
stories.background: The Centre introduced a Delimitation Bill and the Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill in April, linking them to 33 per cent reservation for women. The earlier Bill sought to redraw boundaries using the 2011 Census and raise Lok Sabha seats from 543 to 850. The amendment fell short of a two-thirds majority. Southern opposition parties have opposed delimitation, saying it would reduce their share of seats.
stories.whatNext: The new delimitation Bill is expected to be introduced in the special sitting of Parliament that begins on November 30.

stories.headline: Venezuela's assembly chief says law banning opposition figures will be repealed
stories.dek: Jorge Rodríguez said he expects the reforms to be approved next week, following talks between the interim government and parts of the opposition.
stories.summary: Venezuela will repeal a 2024 law that permanently barred people who backed foreign sanctions from political office, National Assembly head Jorge Rodríguez said. He expects approval next week.
body: Jorge Rodríguez, the head of Venezuela's National Assembly, said on Thursday that the legislature will repeal a law that keeps opposition figures out of public office.

The repeal affects the opposition's room to take part in any future election. Interim president Delcy Rodríguez has promised a free and fair vote but has not set a date. Critics have said the law enabled political persecution.

Known as the Simón Bolívar Law, it was passed shortly after the July 2024 presidential election, which Nicolás Maduro, then president, was declared to have won. There were widespread allegations of fraud. The law permanently banned anyone who requested or supported foreign sanctions on Venezuela from political office and took their assets.

"Legislative processes are dynamic processes. That law responded to a very specific moment in a particular situation that Venezuela was going through," Jorge Rodríguez said. He said no politician had been subjected to its provisions. He said he expected the reforms to be approved next week.

Jorge Rodríguez is the older brother of Delcy Rodríguez. Her interim government has run the country since US forces seized Maduro in January. It has talked with parts of the opposition since August, and the two sides agreed to review several laws as part of a "route map towards democracy", according to an opposition statement. Jorge Rodríguez said the law now being repealed was among those covered.

Opposition leader María Corina Machado, a Nobel Peace Prize laureate, returned to Venezuela in October after more than 10 months in exile. She is widely expected to run in any election, though she is excluded from the talks. Maduro's government had barred her from running in 2024, and her ally Edmundo González stood in her place.

On Thursday, Machado launched neighbourhood assemblies to collect proposals for a future government programme and a democratic transition. Her team said the assemblies are expected to involve over a million people over several months. It told the AFP news agency that about 2,000 meetings were held in Venezuela and abroad on the first day.
"We are designing the transition to democracy, the Venezuelan way," Machado said on social media.
keyFacts: The Simón Bolívar Law was passed shortly after the July 2024 election.
It permanently barred people who backed foreign sanctions from office and confiscated their assets.
Talks between the interim government and parts of the opposition began in August.
Machado's team says about 2,000 assembly meetings were held on the first day.
Machado's assemblies ask 19 questions, with answers fed into a digital platform.
stories.background: An electoral authority closely aligned with the government declared Maduro the winner of the July 2024 election and did not publish detailed tallies. The opposition said González won and uploaded copies of voting tallies as evidence. US forces seized Maduro in January 2026, and Delcy Rodríguez has led an interim government since.
stories.whatNext: Jorge Rodríguez said he expects the National Assembly to approve the reforms next week.

stories.headline: Ajmer land order near Taragarh Fort draws forest-law challenge from environmentalist
stories.dek: Ashok Malik says a revenue order cannot remove forest protection from 5.87 hectares in the Aravallis, where the state plans tourism facilities.
stories.summary: An Ajmer divisional commissioner ordered 5.87 hectares near Taragarh Fort recorded as Rajasthan government land. Environmentalist Ashok Malik says old forest notifications protect the land and wants construction halted until its status is settled.
body: Environmentalist Ashok Malik has challenged an October order that reclassified 5.87 hectares of land near Taragarh Fort in Ajmer's Aravalli hills, saying the land is legally forest and cannot be reclassified by a revenue order.

The land sits where the Rajasthan government plans a tourist destination. Its 2026-27 budget announced parking, gardens, cafés and a museum at Taragarh. Malik says building without forest approvals could end in demolition and extra cost to the public.

On October 6, Ajmer Divisional Commissioner Shakti Singh Rathore directed that the land, in the revenue village of Thok Maliyan, be recorded as Rajasthan government land under the name 'Taragarh Fort Area'. The disputed land covers three zones totalling 58,688 square metres.

The order refers to old forest notifications. Citing a joint survey of June 9, 2022 and existing revenue records, it concluded that the Forest Department's possession of the land had not been established. It noted that parts of the land were already registered to various government departments. It also recorded the Forest Department's position that the land falls under forest notifications.

Malik cited three Forest Department notifications, dated August 11, 1940, March 25, 1950 and June 16, 1951. He also cited a notification of October 6, 2023 declaring the Ganga-Bhairav Valley Conservation Reserve under the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972.
The reserve includes the 468.421-hectare Taragarh Nazul Reserved Forest and the 10.52-hectare Ajmer Taragarh Reserved Forest.
He said documents prepared in December 2021 for a proposed Taragarh passenger ropeway identified parts of the land, registered as Khasra No 6262, as protected forest.

Malik argued that possession and legal status are separate questions. He said Section 2 of the Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980 requires central government approval before forest land is diverted to non-forest use in specified circumstances, and that a change in revenue records does not give that approval. He also cited Section 29(4) of the Rajasthan Forest Act, 1953, saying a revenue official's order cannot replace the legal process for revoking protected forest status.

His representation also cited Supreme Court rulings in the T N Godavarman and Tarun Bharat Sangh cases and a Rajasthan High Court judgment of March 24, 2025 in the Mohammad Yakub case. As a precedent, he pointed to the Seven Wonders Park and food court near Ana Sagar Lake in Ajmer, where demolition began on orders from the National Green Tribunal (NGT) and the Supreme Court.

On November 13, Malik submitted the representation to the Ajmer Development Authority and Ajmer Municipal Corporation. He asked them to stop construction, excavation, tree felling and land clearing, and to order a joint survey by the Forest and Revenue Departments. He also asked for the project's plans, approvals, work orders and forest clearance documents to be made public.
He has sought a reply within seven days of receipt. He said he would approach the NGT's Bhopal bench if work proceeds without the necessary approvals.
keyFacts: The disputed land is in Thok Maliyan revenue village, Ajmer, and covers three zones.
Malik cites forest notifications from 1940, 1950 and 1951.
The Ganga-Bhairav Valley Conservation Reserve was notified on October 6, 2023.
The order relied on a joint survey conducted on June 9, 2022.
Malik wants a reply from the two civic bodies within seven days.
stories.background: Taragarh Fort stands on a hill in the Aravalli range near Ajmer. Forest land cannot be put to non-forest use without central government approval in specified circumstances under the Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980. Revenue records and forest notifications are kept by different departments, which has produced boundary disputes.
stories.whatNext: Malik has asked the Ajmer Development Authority and Municipal Corporation to reply within seven days of receiving his representation, failing which he says he will approach the NGT's Bhopal bench.

stories.headline: GCC begins piling work for Kodungaiyur waste-to-energy plant as residents object
stories.dek: Chennai's civic body says 15 of 400 piles are done at the 21 MW plant; a residents' federation says it was promised no work before a public hearing.
stories.summary: The Greater Chennai Corporation has started piling work for a 21 MW waste-to-energy plant at the Kodungaiyur dumpyard after getting preliminary consent from the pollution board. Residents' groups oppose the project and say they will protest.
body: The Greater Chennai Corporation (GCC) has begun preliminary piling work for a 21 MW waste-to-energy incinerator at the Kodungaiyur dumpyard, after getting a Consent to Establish for the preliminary works from the Tamil Nadu Pollution Control Board.

The plant will burn 1,400 tonnes of dry municipal waste a day. It is meant to take waste from eight zones of north and west Chennai, including Tiruvottiyur, Manali, Madhavaram, Tondiarpet, Royapuram, Thiru Vi Ka Nagar, Ambattur and Anna Nagar.

A GCC official said the consent was obtained on August 24, and land levelling and the access road are complete. Pile foundation work is under way, with 15 of 400 piles done. The official said the rest should be finished by January 2027.

The plant is the first phase of a larger Integrated Waste Processing Facility. GCC is providing 74 acres and spending Rs 1,268.38 crore under a design-build-finance-operate-transfer model, a public-private partnership. The full facility is meant to process 3,700 tonnes a day and generate 36 MW.

Phase I also includes 300 tonnes a day through Bio-CNG and 1,300 tonnes through material recovery and composting. Phase 2 would add a 700 tonne incinerator generating 15 MW, the official said. Phase I is expected to be completed by December 2028, followed by 25 years of operation and maintenance.

TK Shanmugam, president of the Federation of North Chennai Residents Welfare Association, said the corporation had assured residents in two official letters and in meetings with the Mayor and the Commissioner that no work would start until a public opinion survey, a public hearing and Pollution Control Board clearance were completed.
"Residents will take all necessary steps to block and halt the project, including a larger-scale protest if the government proceeds," Shanmugam said.

J Prasanth of the Chennai Climate Action Group said the site is a wetland and that levelling it with debris would increase flooding in North Chennai. He cited a Palliyur Trust report that says 54 bird species live in the area.

GCC Commissioner GS Sameeran said the plant is similar to major projects in India and abroad and complies with Central Pollution Control Board and state board rules. "If we follow these guidelines, we can prevent hazards," he said.
GCC has also proposed Rs 63.87 crore under the Union housing ministry's Urban Challenge Fund for boundary walls, access roads, water supply and power evacuation.
keyFacts: Consent to Establish for preliminary works was obtained from the pollution board on August 24.
GCC is providing 74 acres and spending Rs 1,268.38 crore on the facility.
Phase 2 would add a 700 tonne incinerator generating 15 MW.
GCC has proposed Rs 63.87 crore under the Urban Challenge Fund.
stories.background: The Kodungaiyur dumpyard receives municipal solid waste from north Chennai. GCC plans an integrated facility there to process 3,700 tonnes a day in two phases, with incineration, Bio-CNG and composting units.
stories.whatNext: GCC expects the remaining pile work to be finished by January 2027 and the first phase by December 2028.
