stories.headline: Telangana HC brings in CBI over SBI's ₹500 crore loan to Sem India Fab
stories.dek: Justice Nagesh Bheemapaka said the court could not understand why the bank lent such a sum in 2011, a year after the government began resuming the company's land.
stories.summary: The Telangana High Court on Friday impleaded the CBI's Hyderabad unit to assist it in a petition by SBI over ₹500 crore in loans to Sem India Fab. The judge questioned the bank's due diligence and listed the case for December 4.
body: The Telangana High Court on Friday, on its own motion, made the Central Bureau of Investigation's Hyderabad unit a party to a petition by the State Bank of India over loans of nearly ₹500 crore to Sem India Fab Private Limited.
The case concerns public money lent to a company that was to build a semiconductor plant near Hyderabad. The court has asked the CBI to assist it in examining how the loan was sanctioned.

Justice Nagesh Bheemapaka said it was the bank's legal duty to exercise due diligence when it assessed the company's revenue and sources of loan repayment. "It was the legal duty of the bank to exercise due diligence while assessing the revenue/loan repayment sources of the company at the time of advancing a humongous loan of ₹500 crore," he said.

The judge noted that the bank lent the money in 2011, a year after the government issued resumption proceedings against the company's land. He said it was "incomprehensible to this Court" why the bank advanced such a loan.
The SBI says it lent the money relying on no-objection certificates the government issued in 2009. These allowed the company to mortgage its leasehold interest in the land.

In 2006, the government of undivided Andhra Pradesh signed a Memorandum of Understanding with the company for an assembling, testing, marketing and packing semiconductor plant at Fabcity in Hyderabad. In 2007, it leased the company 100 acres at Raviryala in Maheshwaram mandal for 66 years. The company was to invest 2.25 billion US dollars.
In 2010, the government cancelled the allotment of 78 acres because it was dissatisfied with progress. The company kept the remaining 22 acres on revised lease conditions.

The company challenged the resumption in the High Court, which upheld the government's decision. It also went to court over the bank's notice to auction its land, and the court stayed the auction. The bank's review petition against that was dismissed.
The SBI then filed the present writ petition. It seeks a direction to stop the government's 2023 proceedings to take back land from the company.
The judge directed the Registry to hand all relevant documents to the CBI's standing counsel.
keyFacts: The loan was advanced to Sem India Fab in 2011.
The government leased 100 acres at Raviryala to the company in 2007.
The government cancelled the allotment of 78 acres in 2010.
The company had proposed investment of 2.25 billion US dollars in the plant.
stories.background: In 2006 the undivided Andhra Pradesh government signed an agreement with Sem India Fab for a semiconductor assembly and testing plant. The land allotment was partly cancelled in 2010. The High Court upheld that decision, and later stayed the bank's auction of the company's land.
stories.whatNext: The High Court has adjourned the matter to December 4.

stories.headline: Gargai dam gets wildlife board clearance; BMC aims for 440 MLD by 2029
stories.dek: The Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation still needs two forest clearances and rehabilitation approvals before it can begin construction, which it hopes to do in early 2027.
stories.summary: The National Board for Wildlife's Standing Committee has cleared the Gargai dam project in Palghar district. The BMC plans to start building in early 2027 and to supply an extra 440 million litres a day to Mumbai from the 2029 monsoon.
body: The National Board for Wildlife's Standing Committee has granted wildlife clearance to the Gargai dam project in Palghar district, the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) said.

The dam is meant to add 440 million litres per day (MLD) to Mumbai's water supply. The BMC now supplies about 4,100 MLD from seven lakes. Demand is estimated at 4,463 MLD and is projected to reach 6,900 MLD by 2041.

The committee met in Delhi on Monday under the Union Environment Minister. "This was one of the crucial permissions we have received. We are now awaiting the official minutes of the meeting," a senior civic official said.

The BMC still needs two forest clearances, one from the Maharashtra government and one from the Centre. Land requirements, compensatory afforestation and approvals for the rehabilitation of affected villages must also be completed. The official said the BMC expects these within two months.
The civic body has begun moving machinery and workers to the site. It aims to finish the dam and related structures by May-June 2029 and to start storing and supplying water by the 2029 monsoon.

The BMC plans to build the main dam in nine months. The Middle Vaitarna dam took 15 months. The Central Design Organisation in Nashik, the state's top technical body for dam construction, has cleared the basic design and structural aspects. The dam will use roller-compacted concrete.
The project is in Wada taluka. It involves a 69-metre-high dam near Ogada village and a 2.2-km tunnel to carry water to the Modak Sagar reservoir.
It will require felling around 3.1 lakh trees, including in parts of the Tansa Wildlife Sanctuary. This calls for compensatory planting on non-forest land.
About 34 per cent of the water supplied in Mumbai is reportedly lost to leakage and theft. Moving villagers is expected to begin once the permissions are in hand, an official said.
keyFacts: The dam will be 69 metres high, near Ogada village in Wada taluka.
A 2.2-km tunnel will carry water to the Modak Sagar reservoir.
About 3.1 lakh trees will need to be felled.
The Middle Vaitarna dam, completed in 2014, is the last major addition to Mumbai's supply.
The BMC plans to complete the dam by May-June 2029.
stories.background: Mumbai gets water from seven lakes: Tansa, Bhatsa, Modak Sagar, Tulsi, Vihar, Upper Vaitarna and Middle Vaitarna. The last major addition was the Middle Vaitarna dam, completed in 2014. Gargai is expected to be the next.
stories.whatNext: The BMC expects the remaining forest and rehabilitation approvals within two months and aims to begin construction in early 2027.

stories.headline: Taiwan votes in local elections as Taipei mayoral race draws close attention
stories.dek: Nearly 20 million people can choose 11,051 officials on Saturday, while China runs a weeks-long landing drill in Fujian province across the Taiwan Strait.
stories.summary: Taiwan holds island-wide local elections on Saturday, with the Taipei mayor's race between KMT incumbent Chiang Wan-an and DPP challenger Puma Shen the most watched contest. China is also running an amphibious landing drill in Fujian, using civilian ships as a floating bridge.
body: Taiwan votes on Saturday, November 28, in local elections to choose mayors, county magistrates, councillors and other officials, with the Taipei mayoral race the most closely watched contest.

Nearly 20 million voters are eligible to elect 11,051 officials. The vote is a first test for both the ruling Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) and the main opposition Kuomintang (KMT) before the 2028 presidential election. The KMT now governs 14 of the 22 cities and counties. The DPP governs five.

In Taipei, the KMT's Chiang Wan-an is seeking re-election against the DPP's Puma Shen, a legislator and academic. The DPP has not held the mayor's office since 1998. Chiang once led comfortably in opinion polls, but Shen has narrowed the gap since September with a campaign called "Ocean Current", a play on his Chinese name.

Shen has focused on urban livability, tree cover, schools, child safety and social welfare. Chiang points to subsidies for couples planning children, expanded temporary childcare, the opening of the Taipei Dome and Nvidia's planned Taiwan headquarters.

China declared Shen a "diehard separatist" in 2024. He is the first candidate under Beijing's sanctions to run for mayor of the capital. Shen said in a recent interview that even a loss would be "a slap to China" because it showed "democracy works here in Taiwan".

Other races are also tight. In New Taipei, which the KMT has governed for 16 years, polls show the DPP's Su Chiao-hui and the KMT's Lee Shu-chuan close. The KMT hopes to make gains in Kaohsiung, a DPP stronghold, with candidate Ko Chih-en.

Campaigns have centred on housing, wages, transport and quality of life. Taiwanese officials have reported thousands of incidents of suspected election misinformation or interference. China's Taiwan affairs office spokesperson Zhu Fenglian said the allegations were "completely fabricated" and aimed to "stir up anti-China sentiment to win votes".

Chu Chao-hsiang, a political science professor at National Taiwan Normal University, said it would be very hard for KMT chairwoman Cheng Li-wun to stay on if the party won fewer than 10 seats. He also cautioned that a DPP win would not guarantee success in 2028.

Separately, China is conducting a weeks-long landing drill in Dacheng Bay in Fujian, about 280 km from Taiwan's main island, according to satellite images and a report by the geospatial firm ingeniSPACE. It was first spotted on November 1 and was still under way on Friday, a senior security official said. The official made no link to the elections.

The images show eight civilian vessels joined into a floating bridge about 800 m long. Taiwan's Defence Ministry said it was aware of the activity and was weighing the implications. China's Defence Ministry has called its training "entirely legitimate and reasonable".
Results are expected on Saturday night. Voters will also decide a referendum on nuclear power.
keyFacts: Taiwan shut down its last operating nuclear reactor in 2025; a referendum on nuclear power is on the ballot.
The DPP won only five local seats in 2022.
Puma Shen, 44, is a criminologist and national legislator.
Taiwan's economy grew by more than 14% in the first nine months of the year.
The Dacheng Bay drill floated a bridge about 800 m long from eight civilian vessels.
stories.background: Taiwan holds local elections every four years. The DPP of President Lai Ching-te won just five seats in 2022, after public dissatisfaction over local governance. The KMT favours closer ties with Beijing, and chairwoman Cheng Li-wun met Chinese leader Xi Jinping this year. China claims Taiwan as its territory and has not ruled out force.
stories.whatNext: Results are expected on Saturday night.

stories.headline: New Zealand reach 246/5 on day one of second Test as Akash Deep takes two
stories.dek: Tom Latham and Tom Blundell scored fifties at Hagley Oval after India chose to bowl, but Akash Deep's spell of two wickets for seven runs briefly pulled India back.
stories.summary: New Zealand finished the first day of the second Test against India in Christchurch on 246 for five. Tom Latham made 59, Tom Blundell is on 53 not out, and Akash Deep took 2 for 52.
body: New Zealand ended the first day of the second Test against India at Hagley Oval, Christchurch, on 246 for five, with Tom Blundell on 53 and Glenn Phillips on 36 not out.
The Test is the last of the series. India captain Shubman Gill won the toss and chose to bowl. With five wickets in hand, New Zealand are placed to build a large first-innings total on Saturday.
India made one change, giving debutant Gurnoor Brar his Test cap in place of Prasidh Krishna. New Zealand named an unchanged side.
New Zealand captain Tom Latham and Devon Conway put on 77 for the first wicket. Latham was 42 not out at lunch. Conway made 31 and was out lbw to Brar off the last ball of the session.

Latham was dropped on 29 by KL Rahul at slip. He went on to make 59 off 128 balls before Akash Deep had him caught behind. Akash Deep also had Rachin Ravindra caught behind for 0, in a spell of 7-4-7-2. Anshul Kamboj dismissed Henry Nicholls, who pulled a short ball to long leg.
Those three wickets fell with no run added, and New Zealand were 110 for four. Daryl Mitchell and Blundell then added 74 for the fifth wicket.
Washington Sundar, brought on in the 61st over, ended that stand. Mitchell, on 31, was caught at leg slip by Dhruv Jurel.
Blundell, playing his 50th Test, and Phillips then added an unbroken 62. Blundell reached his fifty with a steer through point off Jasprit Bumrah. Phillips has 5 fours off 64 balls.
Bumrah bowled 19 overs for 37 runs without a wicket. India took the new ball once it became available, and Akash Deep and Bumrah bowled four overs with it without success.
Akash Deep finished with 2 for 52 in 21 overs. Brar took 1 for 52 in 19 overs.
Kamboj took 1 for 56, and Sundar took 1 for 36.
keyFacts: Latham made 59 off 128 balls; Blundell has 53 off 117 balls.
Three wickets fell at 110, with no run added between them.
Brar became India's 321st Test cricketer.
Bumrah's figures were 19-4-37-0.
Extras contributed 20 runs, including seven no-balls.
stories.background: India and New Zealand are playing a two-Test series. Phillips scored a century for New Zealand in the first Test in Wellington, where India made the highest Test total by a visiting side in New Zealand.
stories.whatNext: Play resumes on Saturday, with India looking to take the remaining five New Zealand wickets.

stories.headline: Yeh Prem Mol Liya and Gunmaaster G9 open slowly as critics split
stories.dek: Ayushmann Khurrana's family drama and Emraan Hashmi's action film, both released on Friday, got mixed reviews and modest first-day figures, with Ramayana still ahead.
stories.summary: Ayushmann Khurrana's Yeh Prem Mol Liya earned ₹4 crore on its first day, according to Sacnilk, while Pinkvilla put Emraan Hashmi's Gunmaaster G9 at ₹3 crore. Reviews of both films were mixed.
body: Ayushmann Khurrana's Yeh Prem Mol Liya and Emraan Hashmi's Gunmaaster G9 both released in theatres on Friday, November 27, and both had slow first days at the box office.

For viewers choosing a weekend film, the two releases face a rival that is already well established. Ramayana, starring Ranbir Kapoor and Yash, collected more than ₹7 crore on its 23rd day, according to the tracker Sacnilk. The film has crossed the ₹1000 crore mark.

Sacnilk put the first-day earnings of Yeh Prem Mol Liya at ₹4 crore across 5,631 shows. Pinkvilla estimated that Gunmaaster G9 opened with ₹3 crore net and called the start poor. It noted that Emraan Hashmi's earlier film this year, Awarapan 2, did well.

Yeh Prem Mol Liya's opening was just below those of Ayushmann's two earlier 2026 releases. Pati Patni Aur Woh Do earned ₹4.10 crore and Udta Teer ₹4 crore on their first days. The film did better than Andhadhun at ₹2.70 crore and Shubh Mangal Saavdhan at ₹2.71 crore. His 2025 film Thamma opened at ₹24 crore.

Yeh Prem Mol Liya is directed by Sooraj Barjatya and also stars Sharvari. It follows Prem, a musician, who moves with his family into the Mumbai home of his bride Purva, a journalist who will not leave the older women who depend on her. The runtime is 173 minutes.

Critics were divided. Rishabh Suri, reviewing for Hindustan Times, gave it three stars and called it a reasonably entertaining watch with old-school charm, though he said it loses steam once the melodrama takes over. The Hindu's reviewer called it a sweet but cautious challenge to marriage customs. Scroll's reviewer said the film sags after the interval and praised Sharvari's performance.

Gunmaaster G9, directed by Aditya Datt, stars Emraan Hashmi as Eeshwar, a dairy business owner with a violent past. A police inspector pushes him to infiltrate a drug gang led by Desu, played by Aparshakti Khurana. Genelia D'Souza and Inayat Verma also star.

Rishabh Suri gave it two stars. He called the story predictable and said it follows the same outline as Awarapan 2, though he praised Aparshakti's villain and Genelia's second-half scenes. The Hindu's reviewer was kinder, saying the film hits more than it misses, but noted that the build-up to Eeshwar's past is thin.

Both films carry music by Himesh Reshammiya. Suri found the songs in Gunmaaster G9 forgettable and the tunes in Yeh Prem Mol Liya beautiful. The Hindu's reviewer found the use of Reshammiya's voice for Ayushmann's character jarring.

stories.headline: Spain votes Sunday as Sánchez fights to hold off PP and Vox
stories.dek: Polls point to the People's Party finishing first but short of a majority, which would leave it needing Vox to govern after the final rallies.
stories.summary: Spain holds a snap general election on Sunday after party leaders held closing rallies on Friday. Polls suggest the conservative PP would need the far-right Vox to govern, a result Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez says he cannot imagine.
body: Spain's prime minister, Pedro Sánchez, said on Friday he was convinced he would secure a left-wing majority in Sunday's general election, despite polls pointing to a win for the right.

The result matters beyond Spain. If the conservative People's Party (PP) needs the far-right Vox party to govern, Vox would enter national government for the first time since democracy returned after the death of Francisco Franco in 1975.

Sánchez, who leads the Socialists (PSOE), called the snap election on October 5. The PP, Vox and the Catalan party Junts had voted down emergency measures the government drew up for a housing crisis. Polls say the PP would finish first but fall short of an absolute majority. Vox is polling at almost 20% of the vote.

The Socialists and their ally, the Broad Front led by Ada Colau, held closing rallies in Madrid. Sánchez has focused on women's rights and has warned that a right-wing government including Vox would roll back past gains. Surveys suggest the Socialists have narrowed the gap, but the left bloc still trails the combined PP and Vox total.

The PP's leader, Alberto Núñez Feijóo, ended his campaign in Seville. Andalusia has 61 of the 350 seats in parliament, more than any other region, and is run by a PP-Vox coalition. Feijóo says he wants to govern with a majority backed by "parliamentary support agreements" with Vox. He says he has never discussed ministerial posts with Vox's leader, Santiago Abascal.
"Governing is about managing, and I have spent my whole life preparing for this moment," Feijóo said in Seville.

In Thursday's televised debate, Feijóo used the word "calladita" about Colau and the left, with a finger to his lips. The word can be used to tell a woman to keep quiet. Sánchez called it sexist and asked for "a little respect". On Friday Feijóo sought to clarify what he meant and accused Colau of staying silent during "these years of corruption".

Vox held its final rally at a bullring in Valencia before thousands of people. Its secretary general, Ignacio Garriga, called for "less burka and less halal" and said he acted out of love for the homeland, not hatred. A small part of the crowd chanted "Viva Franco". Vox, which won 33 seats three years ago, hopes to almost double that total.
Campaigning is banned on Saturday, a day of reflection before voting.
keyFacts: Spain's parliament has 350 seats; Andalusia alone has 61.
Vox won 33 seats in the previous election and is polling at almost 20%.
Sunday's vote is Spain's sixth general election in 11 years.
PP and Vox already govern together in Andalusia, Extremadura, Aragón and Castilla y León.
Pollster 40dB puts women at one for every 1.29 men among Vox supporters, down from 1.7 a year ago.
stories.background: Sánchez has been prime minister since 2018. He won an unlikely victory in a snap election in 2023, helped by women voters. This time he called the vote after right-wing parties blocked emergency housing measures, as protests over rents spread and a general strike drew more than 3 million people.
stories.whatNext: Voting takes place on Sunday, November 29, after Saturday's day of reflection.

stories.headline: Pakistan hosts Saudi Arabia and Turkey for two-day defence pact meeting
stories.dek: Talks in Islamabad are expected to centre on Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia, with Pakistan's army chief and foreign and defence ministers attending.
stories.summary: A two-day meeting of the Saudi-Pakistan-Turkey defence alliance's top committee began in Islamabad on Friday. Discussions are expected to focus on Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia and the wider situation in West Asia.
body: A two-day meeting of the top decision-making committee of the Pakistan-Saudi Arabia-Turkey defence alliance began in Islamabad on Friday, with Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia expected to dominate talks.

The pact treats an armed attack on any one member as an attack on all three. It matters in India because Pakistan, India's neighbour and main military rival, is a party to it. India's foreign ministry has said it values its ties with Saudi Arabia and wants Riyadh to keep New Delhi's concerns in mind.

The gathering is the third session of the Strategic, Political and Defence Committee. Defence Minister Khawaja Asif said the foreign and defence ministers of all three countries would attend. Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar and army chief Field Marshal Asim Munir are also taking part for Pakistan.

Asif called the meeting "very important". He said the "continuous turmoil south of Saudi Arabia will obviously be on the agenda". In his words, "Any threat to Saudi Arabia is a threat to Pakistan and Turkiye according to the pact, which is absolutely clear."

Two Pakistani security officials, who were not authorised to speak publicly, said diplomats and defence and military officials would discuss ways to deter threats, expand military cooperation, share intelligence and strengthen defence industry ties. Pakistan's government has not released details of the agenda.
Authorities declared a public holiday in Islamabad and imposed movement restrictions in Islamabad and Rawalpindi. Traffic police announced road diversions for foreign delegations.

Saudi Arabia has faced repeated attacks from the Iran-backed Houthis of Yemen, who have targeted oil facilities and airports. On Tuesday, a tower in Riyadh's financial district was hit, injuring 11 people, including two Indians and three Nepalese nationals. On Thursday, Saudi Arabia struck western and southwestern Yemen.

Pakistan says the agreement is defensive and not aimed at any country, including Iran. Dar spoke by phone on Thursday with Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi about the regional situation. Pakistan is also working with Qatar and others to urge the United States and Iran to return to talks.

Pakistan's army spokesman, Lt Gen Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry, said earlier this month that Pakistan was ready to take "all necessary defensive measures" to protect Saudi Arabia. Pakistani troops are already stationed in the kingdom, he said, mainly providing defensive support and joining exercises.
keyFacts: The Mecca Joint Defence Agreement was signed in August by Mohammed bin Salman, Recep Tayyip Erdogan and Shehbaz Sharif.
The pact binds members for 10 years, with three months' notice needed to leave afterwards.
Its secretariat is in Saudi Arabia; retired Pakistani General Nauman Mahmood is the first secretary-general.
At an emergency meeting in Riyadh on October 5, members agreed to rapid deployment of forces to Saudi Arabia.
stories.background: Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkey signed the pact in Mecca in August 2026. At an emergency committee meeting in Riyadh on October 5, they agreed to move to practical implementation of collective defence, including rapid deployment of forces to the kingdom. Pakistan brokered an interim deal between the United States and Iran in June 2026 and says it is still pressing both to resume talks.
stories.whatNext: The meeting continues in Islamabad on Saturday.

stories.headline: Rohit Sharma named Mumbai Indians captain for IPL 2027 after Hardik Pandya trade
stories.dek: Pandya has moved to Punjab Kings in a swap for pacer Arshdeep Singh, ending three seasons in which Mumbai won no title.
stories.summary: Mumbai Indians have reappointed Rohit Sharma as captain for IPL 2027, three seasons after replacing him with Hardik Pandya. Pandya was traded to Punjab Kings for Arshdeep Singh before the retention deadline.
body: Mumbai Indians on Friday named Rohit Sharma captain for the 2027 Indian Premier League season, three years after the franchise removed him from the role.

The change matters to the team's fans, who watched Mumbai finish ninth in 2026. Sharma takes over after Hardik Pandya, who replaced him as captain, was traded to Punjab Kings for pacer Arshdeep Singh.
Sharma, who turns 40 next April, last led Mumbai in IPL 2023, when the team lost Qualifier 2 to Gujarat Titans. Pandya was named captain before the 2024 season.

"Mumbai Indians has been a huge part of my life, and leading this team has always been something I have always taken great pride in," Sharma said in a release issued by the franchise. He said talks with team owners Nita Ambani and Akash Ambani about the coming season had been exciting.

"I am ready for the 20th season, to the challenges ahead, and to giving our Paltan plenty of moments to celebrate," he said. "The focus will be on playing our brand of cricket, competing together and enjoying the game."

Sharma is Mumbai's longest-serving captain. He led the franchise in 163 matches across the IPL and Champions League T20, with 93 wins and 70 losses. He captained Mumbai in five IPL finals, in 2013, 2015, 2017, 2019 and 2020, and won all five.

Under Pandya, Mumbai finished last in 2024. They reached the playoffs in 2025 before losing Qualifier 2 to Punjab Kings, then ended 2026 in ninth place. Pandya was booed by home fans in his first season as captain. He told the franchise last year that he was ready to move on, and Mumbai agreed to the swap after reviewing the situation, including the option of retaining him.
Sharma has scored 7,329 runs in 281 IPL matches, with two centuries and 49 fifties. Only Virat Kohli of Royal Challengers Bengaluru has more IPL runs, with 9,336.
Mumbai have ₹32.60 crore left in their purse for the IPL 2027 auction, which will be held in Goa on December 16.

stories.headline: Supreme Court grants bail to former AAP MLA Naresh Balyan in MCOCA case
stories.dek: A bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Aparesh Kumar Singh asked Balyan to cooperate with the trial; the Delhi High Court had refused him bail in August.
stories.summary: The Supreme Court on Friday granted bail to former AAP MLA Naresh Balyan, who is accused under the Maharashtra Control of Organised Crime Act. He had been in custody for nearly two years, and the court directed him to cooperate with the trial.
body: The Supreme Court on Friday granted bail to former Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) MLA Naresh Balyan in a case under the Maharashtra Control of Organised Crime Act (MCOCA).

The law deals with organised crime and has strict bail rules. The order ends a long stay in jail for Balyan, who was arrested by the Delhi Police Crime Branch on December 4, 2024. A bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Aparesh Kumar Singh allowed his appeal against the Delhi High Court's August 3 order refusing bail. It directed him to cooperate with the trial.

Police allege that Balyan helped a crime syndicate run by gangster Kapil Sangwan. They say he identified extortion targets, signed sham property agreements and forced property sales at very low prices. In a charge sheet filed in May, police also alleged that he used his political influence to give the syndicate financial help and to help its members avoid arrest.

Balyan's senior advocate, Vikas Singh, told the court that his client was a victim of "political vendetta" and had been in jail for almost two years. Singh also said key prosecution witnesses had retracted their statements. He said Balyan had himself complained to police of threats from Sangwan and had been given police protection.

Additional Solicitor General Raja Thakare, for the Delhi Police, opposed bail. He said the case involved serious allegations, including land grabbing and extortion. He argued that MCOCA applies based on the activities of the syndicate, not on how many cases are registered against one accused. Police counsel put the number of cases against the syndicate at 19; other accounts of the hearing gave it as over 15.

In August, the High Court said a conversation between Balyan and Sangwan showed an "active criminal nexus". It said his complaints against Sangwan did not cancel out other material against him at this stage. It called his claim of political vendetta "merely in the air and completely unsubstantiated". It also held that long custody alone could not decide bail in serious offences under special laws.

Balyan has denied the allegations and has called the use of MCOCA an abuse of law. He told the High Court there was "no shred of evidence" against him. He was arrested in the MCOCA case on the day a trial court granted him bail in an extortion case.

Delhi High Court refused him bail on August 3, 2026.
The High Court noted 17 FIRs against the alleged syndicate.
Delhi Police filed a charge sheet against Balyan in May.
stories.background: Kapil Sangwan, alias Nandu, is described by police as an absconding gangster who runs a crime syndicate. Balyan was arrested in the MCOCA case on December 4, 2024, after getting bail in an extortion case. In March, a High Court bench criticised the police for delay in the investigation. In August, another bench refused him bail, and he then moved the Supreme Court.

stories.headline: Pinarayi Vijayan demands probe after CM Satheesan says his phone is tapped
stories.dek: The Leader of the Opposition asked the Chief Minister to name who is behind the alleged surveillance and whether the Home Minister knew of it.
stories.summary: Opposition leader Pinarayi Vijayan has demanded a comprehensive investigation after Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan said his phone was tapped. Vijayan asked the government to make the findings public.
body: Leader of the Opposition Pinarayi Vijayan on Friday demanded a comprehensive probe into Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan's claim that his phone is being tapped and that he is under constant surveillance.
The exchange concerns the right to privacy, which the Constitution guarantees to every citizen, and who may be watching the state's leaders and residents.

Vijayan, a CPI(M) Politburo member, made his points in a Facebook post. He said it was surprising that a Chief Minister bound to protect fundamental rights was "trivialising illegal phone tapping and continuous surveillance".

He called it ironic that Satheesan had presented unconstitutional practices as normal on a day marking the Constitution. If the head of the state government's own phone was tapped, Vijayan said, it was a grave security lapse, and the Chief Minister should say who was behind it.

Vijayan said serious allegations had been raised that the phones of Opposition leaders and even members of the Cabinet were being tapped. He alleged that Satheesan was treating the matter lightly instead of ordering an investigation.

He also asked whether illegal surveillance was being carried out with the knowledge of Home Minister Ramesh Chennithala. He described "surveillance politics" as a threat to democratic institutions and civil liberties, and urged the government to order an inquiry at once and publish its findings.

Satheesan, of the Congress, made his remarks on Thursday at a Constitution Day programme in Thiruvananthapuram organised by the Dr B.R. Ambedkar Chair at the University of Kerala. He recalled reading George Orwell's novel Nineteen Eighty-Four in college, which depicts a state watching its citizens. He said it left him tense and insecure for a month.

"But now, I have no tension as I know I am under constant surveillance. There are no secrets. I know my phone is also being tapped. So sometimes I say wrong things to mislead those tapping my phone. Everyone is under surveillance," he said.
Satheesan did not say who he believed was behind the alleged tapping or which agency was involved. He does not hold the home portfolio. The government has not announced any investigation.

stories.headline: Apple removes MiniMax's Talkie chatbot from its App Store in every country
stories.dek: The removal followed an investigation that found characters on the AI companion app sent sexual and abusive messages to children, according to the journalists behind it.
stories.summary: Apple has taken Talkie, a chatbot app from Shanghai-based MiniMax, off its App Store in all countries. It acted after ABC News and the Bureau of Investigative Journalism published findings that the app's AI characters messaged children inappropriately.
body: Apple this week took Talkie, an AI chatbot app made by the Chinese company MiniMax, off its App Store in every country, after journalists alleged its AI characters sent sexualised messages to minors.

Talkie has about 11 million monthly users, and child safety groups and regulators in several countries are watching how such apps treat young people. Research firm Sensor Tower says the app is particularly popular in the US, the Philippines and Mexico.

ABC News and the Bureau of Investigative Journalism reported on Wednesday that characters on Talkie had sent children messages that were sexually inappropriate and abusive. MiniMax and Apple did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

Talkie, launched in 2023, lets users chat with AI-generated characters, often in romantic storylines. It is rated 18+ on both Apple's App Store and Google Play. Depending on the country, the app says users under 14 or under 16 cannot sign up.
Child safety advocates have criticised its age checks. Users simply state their own age, and the app does not check it firmly.
AI companion apps differ from assistants such as ChatGPT or Google's Gemini. They are built to hold longer, more personal conversations, sometimes with ongoing storylines.

Talkie and its Chinese version, Xingye, brought in more than 60 per cent of MiniMax's income in 2024. The company stopped reporting the chatbot share separately this year. It has shifted its focus to AI models for business coding and for handling several kinds of input, such as text and video, after listing in Hong Kong in January.

Regulators elsewhere have also acted on AI and children. In July, China barred intimate relationships with minors on domestic AI companion apps, including Xingye, and told platforms to guard against emotional dependency and addiction. ByteDance and Alibaba have since disabled human-like interactive agents and customised agent features on their apps.

Character.AI, another companion app maker, faces several lawsuits in the US over its chatbots' interactions with minors. Governments criticised Elon Musk's Grok chatbot this year after it was used to create sexualised images of women and children.

stories.headline: I&B ministry asks Netflix to respond in seven days to Sukesh Chandrashekhar's notice
stories.dek: The ministry forwarded the jailed accused's representation on his documentary but has not ordered any delay to the December 18 release.
stories.summary: Jailed accused Sukesh Chandrashekhar has served a legal notice on Netflix seeking to defer a documentary on him. The I&B ministry has asked the platform to respond within seven days but has not ordered a postponement.
body: The Ministry of Information and Broadcasting has asked Netflix to respond within seven days to a representation from Sukesh Chandrashekhar, who wants his documentary delayed.

The series, Love, Scam aur Dhokha: The Sukesh Chandrashekhar Story, is due to stream on December 18. Chandrashekhar is in judicial custody at Mandoli Jail in Delhi and faces criminal trials. His lawyers say a release now could affect his right to a fair trial.

In a letter dated November 27, the ministry forwarded the representation by his lawyer, Anant Malik, to Netflix Entertainment Services India. It asked the platform to examine the issues raised. The letter cites the IT Rules, 2021, and the Code of Ethics for OTT platforms, which provides a three-tier system for handling grievances. It also says OTT platforms must not transmit content prohibited by law and must use due caution and discretion.
The letter was signed by Kshitij Aggarwal, Deputy Director (Digital Media). It does not tell Netflix to stop, postpone or withdraw the documentary.

Separately, Malik, of Anantam Legal, issued a legal notice on November 26 to Netflix Entertainment Services India LLP, Netflix Inc. and the India Today Group entity behind India Today Originals. It also names the directors, Moumita Sen and Niyantha Shekar, and executive producer Chandni Ahlawat Dabas. The notice gives them 72 hours to respond.

The notice says the Rs 200 crore extortion case and events inside Tihar Jail are being tried before a Special MCOCA Court at Rouse Avenue Courts in Delhi, where evidence is still being recorded. It says the makers never approached Chandrashekhar and that his only conviction is under appeal. It says he has pleaded not guilty in the pending cases.

His lawyers want the release, trailers and promotions deferred until prosecution evidence ends. They also seek a pre-release screening for his counsel, disclosure of the people featured, and preservation of footage, scripts and correspondence. They want promotional material calling him a "conman" taken down.

Malik said: "This is not an attempt to silence anyone, and it is not a case against documentaries. It is about timing. A film can be released a few months later and lose nothing. A trial cannot be run twice."
Anantam Legal said Chandrashekhar has also written to the Union Home Ministry and intends to move the Delhi High Court. Netflix has not publicly responded.
keyFacts: Netflix announced the December 18 release on November 26.
The ministry's letter, dated November 27, carries reference number J-11013/19/2025-DM.

Chandrashekhar's lawyers say he plans to approach the Delhi High Court.
The notice asks whether prosecution witnesses or prison officials took part in the documentary.
stories.background: Netflix announced the documentary on November 26. It looks at allegations against Chandrashekhar, including that he ran a network of deception from Tihar Jail and extorted around ₹200 crore from Aditi Singh in 2020-21. Hindustan Times reported he was sentenced to eight years in that case. Actors Jacqueline Fernandez and Nora Fatehi have been drawn into related proceedings.
stories.whatNext: Netflix has seven days from receiving the ministry's letter to respond, and the documentary is scheduled to stream on December 18.

stories.dek: The track, a Hindi version of the Boney M. hit, is the second song released from the film, which opens in cinemas on December 24.
stories.summary: The makers of King released 'Daddy Cool' on November 27, putting Shah Rukh Khan and Kareena Kapoor Khan on screen together for the first time since Ra.One in 2011. The film, directed by Siddharth Anand, releases on December 24.
body: The makers of King released the song 'Daddy Cool' on November 27, featuring Shah Rukh Khan and Kareena Kapoor Khan in their first on-screen pairing since the 2011 film Ra.One.

The song is the second to come out of King, which is Khan's first big-screen release since Dunki in 2023. It is a dance number built on the Boney M. song of the same name, and it was unveiled at Meta's House of Instagram 2026, an event attended by more than 700 content creators. It is available on the YouTube channels of Zee Music Company and T-Series.

Sachin-Jigar composed the new version. Arijit Singh and Shilpa Rao sing it, Kumaar wrote the Hindi lyrics and Vaibhavi Merchant choreographed it. The original was performed by Boney M. and written by Frank Farian and George Reyam.
Khan shared the song on Instagram. "Back with Bebo… song old school, but still cool," he wrote in the caption.

The first song from the film, 'Tu Mil Jaaye', featuring Khan and Deepika Padukone, was released on November 2. Kapoor Khan had first hinted at a special number after that release, Hindustan Times reported.

King is directed by Siddharth Anand and produced by Red Chillies Entertainment and Marflix Pictures. The cast includes Suhana Khan, Abhishek Bachchan, Anil Kapoor, Jackie Shroff, Arshad Warsi, Jaideep Ahlawat and Raghav Juyal. Rani Mukerji, Padukone and Kapoor Khan are to make special appearances.
The film is reportedly inspired by the 1994 French film Léon: The Professional. It is said to follow an ageing assassin, played by Khan, and his young protégé, played by Suhana Khan.
King is scheduled to release in cinemas worldwide on December 24, 2026.

stories.headline: Chennai contractors protest over ₹2,200 crore in unpaid Corporation bills
stories.dek: The Greater Chennai Contractors Welfare Association says bills have gone unpaid for six to 10 months and that civic work has slowed as a result.
stories.summary: Hundreds of contractors protested at Rajarathinam Stadium in Egmore on Thursday, demanding that the Greater Chennai Corporation pay about ₹2,200 crore in pending bills. The civic body says it has asked the state government for funds.
body: Hundreds of contractors protested outside Rajarathinam Stadium in Egmore, Chennai, on Thursday, demanding that the Greater Chennai Corporation (GCC) clear about ₹2,200 crore in pending bills.

The money is owed for civic works that are finished or nearly finished. The Greater Chennai Contractors Welfare Association (GCCWA) organised the protest, with members of the Builders Association of India. Protesters said the delay affects their ability to pay for labour, machinery, GST and bank interest.

Association secretary Rama Rao said bills had not been processed for eight months. Protesters said contractors had been waiting six to 10 months. They said there were no pending bills with the Highways Department or the Public Works Department, and that the delay was confined to the GCC and other local bodies.

Rama Rao said the GCC floated tenders in 2025-26 for works including stormwater drains and park renovations without assessing its finances. "We were unaware of the financial status then, and due to political pressure, we took on all the works. As a result, we are suffering now," he said. He also said the previous government had floated several tenders ahead of the Assembly election.
He said no work had been taken up in the last two months. He said corporation officials told contractors the civic body lacked funds, and asked them to press the state government to release money.

Rama Rao said the association had not been able to meet Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay, who heads the Municipal Administration and Water Supply (MAWS) department. An anonymous contractor said the department should create a special fund to settle dues so that recently tendered park, footpath and building works are not affected.

R Radhakrishnan, a former national president of the Builders Association of India, said contractors were being forced to protest while seeking only payment for completed work. He said Corporation engineers and senior officials should raise the matter with the Commissioner. He urged the state government to step in.

Corporation officials said the civic body had asked the state government to sanction funds and was taking steps to release dues in instalments. In November, the GCC said it had cleared bills worth over ₹1,000 crore in five months. An official said its total pending payments and liabilities stood at ₹2,096 crore.
The GCCWA had submitted a petition on October 24 seeking release of the long-pending bills.
keyFacts: The GCCWA petitioned for release of bills on October 24.
The GCC says it cleared bills worth over ₹1,000 crore in five months.
An official put the GCC's pending payments and liabilities at ₹2,096 crore.
Protesters say no bills are pending with the Highways Department or the PWD.
stories.background: The Greater Chennai Corporation is the city's civic body and awards contracts for roads, drains, parks and footpaths. Contractors say tenders issued in 2025-26 left it with more work than it could pay for. The Municipal Administration and Water Supply Department oversees the Corporation and is headed by Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay.

stories.headline: Police to examine Tirur doctor over fairness cream linked to Areekode kidney case
stories.dek: The probe into an 18-year-old's kidney illness will now cover an allegation that a Trikandiyur clinic doctor prescribed the same cream to several patients for months.
stories.summary: Police investigating an Areekode student's kidney disease, allegedly linked to a mercury-containing fairness cream, will examine a claim that a Tirur-area doctor prescribed it to patients. No patient has filed a complaint against the doctor so far.
body: Police in Malappuram will investigate an allegation that a doctor at a private clinic in Trikandiyur, near Tirur, prescribed a mercury-containing fairness cream to patients for several months.

The claim is part of the inquiry into an 18-year-old degree student from Areekode, who says she developed a serious kidney disease after nearly a year of using a fairness cream bought through Instagram. Many people in Kerala buy such creams online and from local shops, so the case bears on what consumers may be putting on their skin.

The girl was diagnosed with membranous nephropathy, a serious kidney disorder, at Aster MIMS Mother Hospital in Areekode. Doctors there suspected a link to a toxic substance. Medical tests reportedly showed very high mercury levels in her blood. She remains under the care of the hospital's nephrology department.
The cream is reportedly made by a firm based in Kasaragod. Police registered an FIR against its alleged manufacturers after her complaint.

The girl told a section of the media that the Tirur doctor had prescribed the same cream to several people. She said she felt discomfort after using it continuously and consulted another doctor, who told her to stop.

No patient has formally complained against the Tirur doctor. A senior police officer said the team had earlier taken statements from doctors indicating that no medical practitioner was prescribing the cream. Because of the media reports, the police decided to look into the matter further.
"The investigation team will record the girl's statement on Saturday and examine the allegation as part of the ongoing probe into the Areekode incident," the officer said.

Police have not yet identified the actual manufacturers. The officer said a group of people in Kasaragod, suspected of being behind the firm that markets the product in Kerala, is under surveillance. "We expect to arrest those responsible soon," he said.
keyFacts: The Areekode student is 18 and was diagnosed with membranous nephropathy.
Police will record her statement on Saturday.
The cream is reportedly made by a Kasaragod-based firm.
No patient has formally complained against the Tirur doctor so far.
Police say a group in Kasaragod is under surveillance.
stories.background: Kerala's Drugs Control Department has been inspecting cosmetics sold in the state. On September 8, the Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation warned consumers against two Pakistan-made creams, saying tests found heavy metals above permissible limits. Officials in Malappuram have also seized 14 cosmetics sold under one brand for lacking documentation.
stories.whatNext: Police will record the girl's statement on Saturday and then examine the allegation against the doctor.

stories.headline: EC hearing on TMC name and symbol dispute ends without a decision
stories.dek: Kalyan Banerjee, for Mamata Banerjee's faction, objected to fresh documents the Ritabrata Banerjee camp wants to file; another hearing is expected.
stories.summary: The Election Commission heard rival Trinamool Congress factions on the party's name, symbol and funds on Friday but reached no decision. Mamata Banerjee's side opposed a request by the Ritabrata Banerjee faction to submit more documents.
body: The Election Commission on Friday ended a hearing on rival Trinamool Congress factions' claims to the party's name, election symbol and funds without a decision.
The ruling decides which group is recognised as the party and controls its assets. Both factions maintained their claims during the proceedings.

Kalyan Banerjee, who represented Mamata Banerjee's faction, objected to the new documents the Ritabrata Banerjee faction wanted to introduce. He argued that the time the Supreme Court had allowed for filing counter-affidavits and supporting papers was over.

He also questioned why the other faction had filed written submissions instead of a counter-affidavit. Written submissions, he argued, cannot be treated as formal pleadings. He said the faction could not add new facts or legal grounds beyond its original petition. He also said some papers had never been shown to his side.

Ritabrata Banerjee defended his faction's position. He said several legislators had been misled and intimidated into signing documents, and that complaints and FIRs filed by legislators and party workers had been brought to the Commission's notice. He said his faction was ready to submit the relevant documents.
Ritabrata Banerjee also took a swipe at Kalyan Banerjee's arguments, suggesting Mamata Banerjee's faction might not engage him in the next round of proceedings.
The Commission is expected to hold another hearing before it decides which faction is entitled to the party's political identity and associated assets. No date was given.
keyFacts: The hearing took place on Friday, November 27, in the dispute over the TMC's name, symbol and funds.
Kalyan Banerjee argued the Supreme Court's time limit for counter-affidavits had expired.
He said written submissions cannot be treated as formal pleadings.
Ritabrata Banerjee said complaints and FIRs by legislators and party workers had been brought to the Commission's notice.
stories.background: The Election Commission is deciding which of two groups claiming to be the Trinamool Congress is entitled to the party's name, symbol and funds. Mamata Banerjee leads one faction; Ritabrata Banerjee leads the rival group. Both have filed claims before the Commission.
stories.whatNext: The Commission is expected to hold another hearing before delivering its final decision, though no date has been announced.

stories.headline: India beat Malaysia 6-2 to reach Women's Asian Champions Trophy final
stories.dek: Deepika scored twice, and India got five of their six goals from penalty corners, to set up a final against China in Bhopal.
stories.summary: India's women beat Malaysia 6-2 in the semifinal of the Asian Champions Trophy in Bhopal on Friday. Deepika scored twice, and India meet China, who beat Japan 1-0, in the final.
body: India's women beat Malaysia 6-2 in the semifinal of the Women's Asian Champions Trophy in Bhopal on Friday, with Deepika scoring twice to put the hosts into the final.
India, the Asian Games champions, will now play China for the title. China beat Japan 1-0 in the first semifinal, with Heyang Zhang scoring in the last minute.

Five of India's six goals came from penalty corners, a set-piece awarded for a foul inside the defending team's circle. Mumtaz Khan scored from one in the 10th minute to open the scoring at the International Sports Complex.
Navneet Kaur made it 2-0 with a field goal in the 18th minute. She took the ball past Malaysian defender Mohd Khairunnisa after a mistrap and shot low past goalkeeper Nur Zainal.
Deepika scored India's third from a penalty corner in the 25th minute. Malaysia pulled one back two minutes later when Nur Azhar deflected in a penalty corner variation.
Deepika restored the three-goal lead in the 30th minute, and India led 4-1 at half-time. Sportstar reported it was her 10th goal of the tournament.
Sunelita Toppo made it 5-1 in the 33rd minute, scoring the rebound after Zainal saved her first attempt. Nuramirah Zulkifli scored a field goal for Malaysia in the 52nd minute.

Ishika scored India's sixth from a penalty corner late in the match. Deepika Kumari's team-mates had earlier been denied a goal when Navneet's strike in the first quarter was ruled out for a backstick.
In the fifth-place match, South Korea beat Thailand 4-1.
keyFacts: Mumtaz Khan opened the scoring from a penalty corner in the 10th minute.
India led 4-1 at half-time.
Navneet Kaur's first-quarter goal was ruled out for a backstick.
South Korea beat Thailand 4-1 to finish fifth.
China beat Japan 1-0 in the other semifinal.
stories.background: India beat Japan 4-0 on Wednesday to finish top of the league stage with a clean sweep. It was their 13th consecutive win. The team reached fourth place in the FIH rankings, their best.
stories.whatNext: India will play China in the final of the tournament in Bhopal.

stories.headline: Swiss cybersecurity office says AI agents were used in five recent cyberattacks
stories.dek: The Federal Office for Cybersecurity said four of the attacks succeeded, and three of those targeted were operators of critical infrastructure.
stories.summary: Switzerland's Federal Office for Cybersecurity said five cyberattacks in recent days used AI agents against companies and critical infrastructure operators. Four of the attacks succeeded and compromised systems, and the office did not say who was behind them.
body: Five cyberattacks in Switzerland over the last few days used AI agents to target companies and operators of critical infrastructure, the Federal Office for Cybersecurity (BACS) said in a statement on Thursday.

An AI agent is software that can carry out tasks on its own, with little human direction. The statement is an official Swiss confirmation that such tools are being used in real attacks. Critical infrastructure means services a country depends on every day.
BACS said four of the five attacks were successful and that systems were compromised. It did not say which systems were affected or what damage was done.
Three of those targeted were operators of critical infrastructure. Swiss public broadcaster SRF reported that they included providers of electricity, water and telecommunications.
BACS did not say who could be behind the attacks.
The office advised companies to put protection measures in place, including regular cyber tests.
keyFacts: BACS issued its statement on Thursday, November 26.
Four of the five attacks succeeded, according to BACS.
Three critical infrastructure operators were among the targets.
SRF reported the three provide electricity, water and telecommunications.
BACS gave no information on who carried out the attacks.
stories.background: BACS is the Swiss federal government's office for cybersecurity. It issues warnings and advice to companies and operators of key services. Agentic AI refers to systems that can plan and carry out multi-step tasks without a person directing each step.

stories.headline: UK benefits and pensions websites go offline after 'cyber incident'
stories.dek: The Department for Work and Pensions says regular payments continue, but some claimants say money has not arrived and they cannot log required job-search records.
stories.summary: Millions of people in the UK have lost access to online benefits and pensions services after the Department for Work and Pensions took systems offline following a "cyber incident". Downing Street has not ruled out an attempted hack but says there is currently no evidence personal data was lost.
body: The UK government said a "cyber incident" has left millions of people without access to online benefits and pensions services, and Downing Street has not ruled out an attempted hack.

Many people in Britain rely on these services for income. The Department for Work and Pensions (DWP) said it took the digital services down as a "precaution". It said regular benefit and pension payments would still be made.

Downing Street said there was "currently no evidence" that personal data had been lost, and that an investigation was under way. Officials could not rule out the involvement of a "malicious actor" but said there was "no evidence" that other government departments had been targeted in this way.

As of around 12:00 GMT on Friday, the online systems for pensions, universal credit and Pip applications could not be accessed. The "Tell Us Once" system, used to tell government when someone has died, was also down. It was not clear when services would return.

Some claimants said payments had not arrived. Samantha Reah, a single mother of four in Cardiff, said she was missing £1,600. "I rely on the payment today - it's my payday," she said. Georgina Howarth, 30, from Plymouth, said she had to ask her mother for money for food.

Claimants also cannot fill in an online journal that shows they are looking for work, a condition of their benefits. Gemma Barnes, from St Neots in Cambridgeshire, said she feared her payments could be cut. The DWP said people would not be sanctioned over missing journal entries during the incident, and that anyone with payment problems should call the benefit phoneline.

The online application service for Healthy Start, an NHS scheme that helps pregnant women and families with young children buy milk or fruit, was also unavailable. A spokesperson said payments were not interrupted.

David Knott, the UK's former Chief Technology Officer, told BBC Newsnight his "strong suspicion" was that the incident was an attack. He said that taking down citizen-facing services suggested an attack could be mounted "through the front door".

A DWP spokesperson said the department was working with the National Cyber Security Centre and the Government Cyber Coordination Centre to investigate and restore services. The department said it would never message people to ask for bank details or to click on links.
keyFacts: The DWP says regular benefit and pension payments are not affected.
Healthy Start online applications are unavailable, though payments continue.
The National Cyber Security Centre warned earlier this month of a possible rise in cyber incidents.
In April 2025, attackers breached the Legal Aid Agency's online services and accessed personal data.
stories.background: The DWP administers the State Pension and working-age and disability benefits for around 20 million claimants and customers. In April 2025 the government reported a breach of the Legal Aid Agency's online services. Earlier this month, the National Cyber Security Centre urged organisations to strengthen defences as hacking tools become more capable.

stories.headline: Telangana High Court dismisses two PILs against Kukatpally land e-auction
stories.dek: The bench said the petitions raised no public interest issue; the auction covers 3.15 acres of government land at Moosapet meant for truck parking.
stories.summary: The Telangana High Court on Friday dismissed two public interest petitions seeking to suspend the e-auction of 3.15 acres of government land at Moosapet in Kukatpally. The bench said no public interest was involved in the issues raised.
body: The Telangana High Court on Friday dismissed two public interest litigation (PIL) petitions that sought to suspend the e-auction of 3.15 acres of government land at Moosapet in Kukatpally.
The land is meant for truck parking. The dismissal removes the court challenge to the online sale of the plot in Hyderabad.
A bench of Acting Chief Justice P. Sam Koshy and Justice Suddala Chalapathi Rao pronounced the order. The bench said there was no public interest involved in the issues the petitioners had raised.

A PIL is a case that a person or group brings in court on a matter of wider public concern, rather than for a personal grievance. Courts can dismiss such petitions if they find no public interest in them.
The material available does not say who the petitioners were, what grounds they gave, or when the e-auction is to be held.

The land is government land meant for truck parking.
The bench comprised Acting Chief Justice P. Sam Koshy and Justice Suddala Chalapathi Rao.
Two PIL petitions were dismissed on Friday, November 27.

stories.headline: Bombay HC holds back mangrove permission for BKC transit project until state files report
stories.dek: The court wants figures on tree cover, losses and five-year survival rates, and said planting must be finished before clearances are sought.
stories.summary: The Bombay High Court has withheld permission for MMRDA's Automated Rapid Transit System in Bandra-Kurla Complex until the state reports on mangrove loss and compensation. The court said it does not oppose the project but will not move ahead without full compliance.
body: The Bombay High Court has withheld permission for a transit project in Mumbai until the Maharashtra government files a detailed report on steps taken to make up for the loss of mangroves.

The Mumbai Metropolitan Region Development Authority (MMRDA) wants to build an Automated Rapid Transit System, 8.85 km long, in the Bandra-Kurla Complex area. A 2018 High Court ruling requires court approval for any development that affects wetlands.

A Bench of Chief Justice Mahesh C. Tripathi and Justice Advait Sethna heard the MMRDA's request to use 0.2869 hectares of mangrove land for the work. The project will not need mangroves to be cleared, but it affects six trees. Planting 100 trees is required as compensation.
The court said afforestation, meaning planting trees to offset losses, must be completed before clearances are sought. It said the exercise cannot be a box-ticking step.

Advocate Saket Mone, appearing for the MMRDA, argued that the system meets key connectivity needs. He said tree planting is the Forest Department's responsibility. The Bench asked why officials had not begun remedial action when the project was first planned.
Advocate General of Maharashtra Milind Sathe attributed the planting delays to a shortage of saline land. He said saplings must be planted before the monsoon if they are to survive.
The Bench pointed to a gap between what regulators file and what is happening on the ground. It asked how authorities could grant permission when rules require 30% tree cover.

The court directed the state to submit figures on tree cover, losses and five-year survival rates before any orders are passed. It said it does not oppose the project but will not proceed without full compliance.
keyFacts: The MMRDA seeks to use 0.2869 hectares of mangrove land in the Bandra-Kurla Complex.
The transit system would cover 8.85 km.
The project affects six trees and needs 100 trees as compensation.
The court cited a rule requiring 30% tree cover.
Mone appeared for the MMRDA; Sathe for the state.
stories.background: A 2018 Bombay High Court ruling requires the court's approval for any development that affects wetlands, including mangrove areas. The MMRDA is the body that plans and builds major infrastructure projects in the Mumbai region.
stories.whatNext: The court has listed the matter for November 30.

stories.headline: BEST workers protest at Azad Maidan, warn of strike from December 21
stories.dek: The union will hold a ballot on December 4 to decide whether to launch an indefinite strike over pending wage and service demands.
stories.summary: Permanent and wet-lease BEST employees protested at Mumbai's Azad Maidan on Friday over pending wage and service-related demands. The union will ballot members on December 4 on whether to begin an indefinite strike on December 21.
body: Permanent and wet-lease employees of the Brihanmumbai Electric Supply and Transport (BEST) undertaking staged a protest at Azad Maidan in Mumbai on Friday, warning of a strike from December 21.
A strike would affect the city's bus commuters, who depend on BEST services. Wet-lease buses are those that the undertaking hires from private operators, along with their drivers.
The BEST Workers' Union said the protest was held to press for the fulfilment of its demands. The workers are seeking changes to pending wage and service-related matters.
The union will conduct a ballot on December 4 to seek the opinion of permanent and waitlisted employees. The vote will decide whether to go ahead with the proposed indefinite strike.
The material available does not say how the BEST administration or the state government responded to the protest, or what specific wage figures the workers are seeking.
keyFacts: The protest took place at Azad Maidan, Mumbai, on Friday, November 27.
Both permanent and wet-lease BEST employees took part.
The union will hold a ballot on December 4.
The proposed indefinite strike would begin on December 21.
stories.background: BEST is the public body that runs bus services in Mumbai. Part of its fleet is operated through wet-lease contracts with private operators, so its workforce includes both permanent staff and staff on such buses.

stories.headline: BMC standing committee clears 15-year deal with Raymond for Worli helipad
stories.dek: Raymond will pay the civic body at least ₹5 lakh a month and bear all costs of converting the Coastal Road construction jetty.
stories.summary: The BMC standing committee on Thursday approved a 15-year public-private partnership with Raymond Ltd to turn the Worli jetty into a DGCA-licensed helipad. The civic body expects a minimum of ₹5 lakh a month without spending municipal funds.
body: The Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation's standing committee on Thursday cleared a 15-year public-private partnership with Raymond Ltd to convert the Worli jetty into a helipad licensed by the Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA).
The civic body expects to earn at least ₹5 lakh every month. It will put no municipal money into building or running the facility.

Raymond will pay a fixed ₹1 lakh a month. The BMC will also receive 50% of revenue from commercial helicopter landings and takeoffs, with a minimum guarantee of ₹4 lakh a month. Earnings could rise with more flights.

Raymond will pay for modifying the structure, obtaining statutory permissions and the DGCA licence, and running and maintaining the helipad. It will also be responsible for safety, emergency response, aircraft rescue and firefighting, and environmental compliance.

The helipad is planned as a multipurpose facility. Uses include medical evacuations, coastal surveillance, security patrols, disaster response with the National Disaster Response Force (NDRF), and movement of VIPs and VVIPs. Flights carrying the chief minister or governor, medical evacuations and NDRF operations will get priority.
The jetty lies about 120 metres offshore, opposite Worli Dairy. It was built as a temporary structure to carry construction material for the Coastal Road (South) project, which is now operational.

IIT-Bombay assessed the structure's stability in June 2024, through the Maharashtra Maritime Board. A separate feasibility study by Pawan Hans Ltd found it suitable for mid-level helicopters under DGCA rules.
The BMC invited Expressions of Interest in December 2025 and received proposals from Raymond and the JSW group.
keyFacts: The agreement runs for 15 years.
Minimum monthly payment to the BMC is ₹5 lakh: ₹1 lakh fixed plus a ₹4 lakh revenue-share guarantee.
The BMC gets 50% of revenue from commercial helicopter landings and takeoffs.
Raymond and the JSW group responded to the December 2025 Expression of Interest.
Pawan Hans Ltd found the site suitable for mid-level helicopters.
stories.background: The Worli jetty was one of two temporary structures built in the first phase of the Mumbai Coastal Road project. The one near Amarsons Garden was later demolished. The Worli jetty was kept after the coastal police asked for it for surveillance. In March 2025, Deputy Chief Minister Eknath Shinde asked the BMC to examine developing a helicopter landing facility along the Coastal Road.

stories.headline: Nvidia chip sellers tell neocloud firms to stop serving Chinese customers
stories.dek: The warning goes further than a US rule in force since November 19, and Nvidia has also put some Southeast Asian chip orders on hold.
stories.summary: Companies that sell Nvidia's advanced AI chips have told specialised cloud providers they risk losing supply if they rent computing capacity to Chinese firms, CNBC reported. It follows a new US rule on remote access to chips.
body: Companies that sell Nvidia's advanced AI chips have told "neocloud" providers to exclude Chinese firms from their customers if they want to keep buying the chips, CNBC reported on Thursday.

Neoclouds are specialised cloud companies. They run data centres full of graphics processing units, or GPUs, and rent that computing power to businesses that build and run AI tools. Their business depends on keeping costly chips in constant use, so losing supply or customers matters to them.

The warning was passed on after the Trump administration announced new restrictions on November 16. The US Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security issued them as an interim final rule, a rule that takes effect before the usual comment period ends. It came into force on November 19.

Earlier US controls had effectively barred Chinese companies from buying Nvidia's most advanced chips. Chinese firms could still rent the computing power of those chips from data centres in other countries. The new rule is meant to close that route. Covered overseas data centres now need a US licence to give Chinese companies significant computing capacity based on advanced US chips.

The sellers' message goes beyond the rule, CNBC reported. It applies even if only part of a neocloud's capacity goes to Chinese customers. Before the rule, Nvidia had said it would not sell chips to customers that rented more than 50 per cent of their GPUs to Chinese companies.

US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer told CNBC the rules were meant to "close off indirect access, either smuggling through places like Southeast Asia or remote access from data centers in third countries."
Two of three people familiar with the matter told CNBC that chip sellers appeared to be looking for new buyers for GPUs meant for data centres that would have served Chinese customers.

Separately, the New York Times reported that Nvidia has put on hold some orders of its most advanced chips from data centre operators in Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia. It cited two people with knowledge of the matter. Nvidia did not immediately comment. The Times said a Commerce Department proposal covering Southeast Asian countries is still under review.

Nvidia has also warned customers about the proposed Remote Access Security Act, which has passed the US House of Representatives but not the Senate. The company said the bill would give the US government wider power over access to cloud services and could expose cloud providers and their customers to legal action.
keyFacts: The US rule on remote access to advanced chips took effect on November 19.
Nvidia earlier said it would not sell to customers renting over 50 per cent of GPUs to Chinese firms.
Orders in Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia are reportedly on hold.
The Remote Access Security Act has passed the House but awaits Senate approval.
stories.background: US export controls have for years restricted sales of Nvidia's most advanced AI chips to China. Chinese firms found a workaround by renting chip capacity from data centres abroad. The November rule targets that route. Washington has also added Singapore-based Megaspeed and other firms to its entity list, a trade blacklist, over suspected chip diversion.
stories.whatNext: The Remote Access Security Act awaits a vote in the US Senate.

stories.headline: Allahabad High Court asks UPPSC to explain how it vets medical college professor selections
stories.dek: The commission's counsel told the court its recommendations will not be given effect until it reports on examiner integrity safeguards, according to the order dated November 25.
stories.summary: The Allahabad High Court has asked the Uttar Pradesh Public Service Commission to disclose its integrity safeguards for selecting professors at government medical colleges. The commission's counsel told the court its recommendations will not be given effect until it reports compliance.
body: The Allahabad High Court has asked the Uttar Pradesh Public Service Commission (UPPSC) to show how it keeps examiners and candidates free of influence when picking medical college professors, LiveLaw reported on Friday.
The order bears on public appointments in Uttar Pradesh. The court is already hearing a petition on the failure to fill regular faculty posts in the state's government medical and nursing colleges.

In its order dated November 25, Justice Siddharth Nandan directed the UPPSC Secretary to say whether examiners gave undertakings that their integrity is of the highest standards and that the candidates were not known to them. The court also asked whether candidates had to disclose past findings of misconduct or pending inquiries.

The order notes that the Secretary's affidavit did not disclose the criteria that ensure transparency and integrity of the selection panel. The court said appointments should follow the prescribed procedure and "inspire confidence".

The commission was told to check the records of recommended candidates and ask their parent institutions whether any misconduct inquiry is pending or whether they were earlier found guilty. It must also examine whether complaints against them were considered before the recommendations were issued.
The court said recommendations could be reconsidered if non-disclosure is found. It said an examiner could be debarred if allegations against him or her are found to be true.

The order records a submission by the commission's counsel. Until UPPSC reports compliance with Paragraph 9 of Chapter IV of the 1985 Act, and subject to further orders, its recommendations will not be given effect.

If the report is not filed by the next date, the Secretary must appear in person. He must bring the records of the appointed examiners, the declarations taken from them before the interviews, and details of complaints against examiners or candidates.

The court made Sanjay Shrinet, the then UPPSC Chairman, a party to the case. It observed that he was at the helm when the recommendations were issued, "just few days before his retirement, in much hurry". He is to be served the petition and the order-sheet so he can respond. His response is not in the report of the order.

The court also questioned the commission's stand that only electronic requisitions will now be entertained, although the state forwarded its requisition in 2021. The commission's counsel could not say whether the government order on e-requisitions applies to past or only future requests.

In the wider case, the bench was told that 26 professor posts are occupied out of 108 to be filled by direct recruitment, with the rest vacant. The court called the state's affidavit on a proposed recruitment board vague and "an eye-wash".
keyFacts: The Director General, Medical Education and Training, said 517 professor posts are sanctioned; 108 are for direct recruitment.
The state said 44 professor posts have been advertised; requisitions for 23 more are yet to be advertised.
The court earlier noted more than 500 contractual incumbents and about 25% of positions managed by officiating Principals.
A copy of the order must go to the State Government within 48 hours.
The recruitment board was contemplated under a Government Order dated January 30, 2026.
stories.background: The court is hearing a writ petition on the failure to fill regular faculty posts in Uttar Pradesh's government medical and nursing colleges. It has earlier noted that hardly 2-3% of posts were shown as held on a regular basis.
stories.whatNext: The matter is listed for further hearing on December 8 at 2:00 PM.
